description: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) ? SHAPE ? \* MERGEFORMAT EMPANELMENT OF DEVELOPMENT & IMPLEMENTATION PARTNERS FOR CSR, COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT & INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS ACROSS INDIA RFP No.: AROH/RFP/2026-27/001 Particular Details Issuing Organisation AROH Foundation Registered/Corporate Office F-52, Sector-8, Noida, Uttar Pradesh Date of Issue August 26, 2026 Last Date for Queries September 24, 2026 Last Date for Submission September 25, 2026 Proposal Validity 90 days from the last date of submission Submission Mode Electronic submission to procurement@aroh.in Empanelment Period As specified in the Letter of Empanelment / onboarding communication This RFP is issued for empanelment only. Empanelment does not create any entitlement to a work order, minimum business volume, exclusivity or reimbursement of proposal preparation costs. 1. INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND AROH Foundation invites proposals from experienced, technically competent and financially sound development agencies, implementation partners, contractors, service providers and vendors for empanelment to undertake CSR, community development, infrastructure, renewable energy, water conservation, natural resource management and allied development projects across India. The RFP is intended to establish a pre-qualified pool of agencies that can be considered for project-specific assignments in accordance with AROH Foundation’s procurement procedures and the requirements of its CSR, donor, government and institutional partners. AROH Foundation intends to create a reliable and technically capable partner ecosystem covering planning, design support, procurement, supply, installation, construction, testing, commissioning, operation and maintenance, capacity building and other implementation services, as applicable to individual projects. Empanelment is a pre-qualification mechanism. An empanelled agency may subsequently be invited to participate in project-specific RFQs, limited bids, competitive quotations, technical-commercial evaluations or other procurement processes. Empanelment shall not constitute a commitment to award any work, any minimum business volume, exclusivity or a right to participate in every future procurement. 2. OBJECTIVE OF THE RFP The objectives of this RFP are to: identify agencies with demonstrated technical, managerial, financial and operational capability; create category-wise and geography-wise pools of qualified implementation partners; enable faster and more competitive procurement for project-specific requirements while maintaining appropriate due diligence and quality standards; secure reliable implementation capacity in rural, remote, tribal, hilly, North-Eastern, Himalayan and other difficult-toaccess locations; and establish a transparent basis for subsequent allocation of work based on technical suitability, experience, capacity, geography, past performance, commercial competitiveness and project requirements. 3. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION Term Meaning AROH / Foundation AROH Foundation, the issuing and contracting organisation. Applicant / Bidder The legal entity submitting a proposal in response to this RFP. Empanelled Agency / Partner A bidder selected and formally empanelled by AROH Foundation under this RFP. Project / Assignment A specific activity or package of work for which an empanelled agency may subsequently be engaged. Work Order / Contract The written instrument issued/executed for a specific assignment, including its scope, BOQ, specifications, price, schedule and conditions. RFQ Request for Quotation or equivalent project-specific commercial solicitation. BOQ Bill of Quantities, where applicable. DLP Defect Liability Period, as specified in the applicable Work Order/Contract. O&M Operation and Maintenance services, where included in the scope. Unless the context otherwise requires, words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa. Section headings are for convenience and do not limit interpretation. 4. SCOPE OF EMPANELMENT Agencies may apply for one or more categories. AROH Foundation may empanel multiple agencies in the same category and may add, modify or refine categories in future procurements based on programme requirements. A. Renewable Energy & Solar Projects Solar PV systems and decentralised solar solutions Solar street lighting Solar water pumping and solar irrigation systems Solar-powered drinking-water systems Solar systems for schools, institutions and community facilities Solar-powered livelihood infrastructure Supply, installation, testing and commissioning (SITC) Electrical and allied works Operation and maintenance of solar installations Other renewable-energy and clean-energy interventions B. School, Anganwadi & Education Infrastructure Classroom renovation and refurbishment School and institutional infrastructure improvement Smart classrooms and digital learning infrastructure Smart Anganwadi Centres STEM/Science Labs and Mini Science Centres Libraries and learning spaces Civil, electrical, plumbing and allied works Furniture and fixtures Other education-related infrastructure C. Water Resource Development & Conservation Community drinking-water infrastructure Water supply and distribution systems Rainwater harvesting Groundwater recharge structures Check dams and related watershed structures Farm ponds and water storage Pond rejuvenation Irrigation-related infrastructure Drainage and water conservation works Other community water-security interventions D. Natural Resource Management & Climate Resilience Watershed development Soil and moisture conservation Land and water resource development Farm-level water conservation Drainage and erosion-control measures Climate-resilient community infrastructure Plantation and ecological restoration-related infrastructure Environmental sustainability interventions Other NRM and climate-resilience activities E. Civil Construction & Community Infrastructure Construction of community infrastructure Renovation, refurbishment, repair and maintenance Community centres and public utility infrastructure Boundary walls and site development Masonry and RCC works Plumbing, electrical and allied works Structural and non-structural repairs Other civil and infrastructure works associated with CSR projects F. Other CSR & Community Development Works Livelihood-supporting infrastructure Community development and public-use assets Environmental sustainability interventions Capacity-building or implementation support linked to physical/community assets Other project-specific CSR and community-development works approved by AROH Foundation The above scope is indicative and non-exhaustive. Individual Work Orders/Contracts shall define the exact scope, specifications, deliverables, BOQ, service levels, completion schedule, testing requirements, warranty/DLP and payment terms. No bidder shall assume that inclusion of an activity in this RFP constitutes an obligation on AROH Foundation to procure that activity. title: Assistant Manager – Human Resources
sectors: Administration, HR, Management, Accounting/Finance
description: Assistant Manager – Human Resources New Delhi A Public Health Consulting Organization We are a health systems consulting organization dedicated to strengthening public health outcomes across India. We partner with government agencies, healthcare providers, development organizations, academic institutions, and funding partners to address complex public health challenges through practical, evidence-based solutions. Our work spans health systems strengthening, primary healthcare, digital health, environmental health, mental health, nutrition, and emergency response, with a strong focus on improving the health of women and children. Combining technical expertise with implementation experience, we help partners translate strategy into measurable impact. Operating as a professional consulting organization, we deliver high-quality advisory and implementation support with agility, rigor, and a commitment to sustainable health outcomes for communities across India. Position Summary The Assistant Manager – Human Resources will be responsible for managing end-to-end HR operations and establishing robust HR systems, policies, controls, and compliance frameworks for the Company. The role will support organizational growth by ensuring effective talent management, employee engagement, statutory compliance, governance, audit readiness, and people-related risk management. The incumbent will function as a key HR business partner and compliance focal point, ensuring that all people practices are aligned with organizational policies, applicable labour laws, regulatory requirements, and governance standards. Reports To: Executive Director Key Responsibilities 1. HR Operations & Employee Lifecycle Management • Manage the complete employee lifecycle including recruitment, onboarding, confirmation, promotion, transfer, contract management, separation, and post-employment documentation. • Ensure maintenance of accurate employee records and personnel files. • Oversee issuance of employment contracts, amendments, offer letters, confirmation letters, promotion letters, and separation documentation. • Ensure timely completion of background verification, induction, and employee onboarding processes. • Coordinate employee exits, full-and-final settlements, and exit interviews. 2. Talent Acquisition & Workforce Planning • Lead end-to-end recruitment processes for approved positions. • Coordinate workforce planning and staffing activities in consultation with department heads. • Develop and update job descriptions and organizational structures. • Manage candidate sourcing, screening, interviewing, selection, and onboarding activities. • Build talent pipelines for critical and hard-to-fill positions. • Maintain recruitment metrics and hiring dashboards. 3. Compensation, Benefits & Payroll Administration • Coordinate payroll inputs and monthly payroll validation. • Ensure administration of employee compensation, benefits, insurance, and welfare programs. • Support annual compensation reviews, promotions, and salary revision exercises. • Manage employee benefit programs including health insurance, gratuity, and retirement benefits. • Support compensation benchmarking and salary structure reviews. • Ensure timely and accurate processing of final settlements. 4. HR Compliance, Labor Law Management & Audit Readiness • Ensure compliance with all applicable labour laws, employment regulations, and statutory requirements. • Develop and maintain an HR compliance calendar to monitor all statutory obligations. • Coordinate compliance relating to: o Provident Fund (PF) o Employee State Insurance (ESI) o Gratuity o Bonus o Professional Tax o Shops & Establishments Act o POSH Act o Labor Welfare requirements o Social Security obligations o Applicable provisions under new labour codes as and when notified • Maintain all statutory registers, records, notices, returns, and documentation. • Conduct periodic HR compliance reviews and compliance risk assessments. • Coordinate labour law audits, internal audits, and statutory inspections. • Ensure closure of audit observations and compliance action items within agreed timelines. • Serve as the focal point for HR compliance documentation and regulatory reviews. • Keep management informed of changes in labour laws and recommend required policy updates. 5. Governance, Policies & Internal Controls • Support development, implementation, and periodic review of HR policies, SOPs, employee handbook provisions, and HR governance frameworks. • Ensure consistent application of organizational policies and employment practices. • Develop and maintain HR controls to reduce compliance and operational risks. • Establish systems for policy communication, employee awareness, and compliance monitoring. 6. Performance Management & Talent Development • Administer performance management processes including goal setting, mid-year reviews, annual appraisals, and development planning. • Support managers in managing underperformance and implementation of Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs). • Support succession planning and talent review exercises. 7. Learning, Development & Compliance Training • Coordinate learning and development initiatives across the organization. • Track completion of mandatory compliance training programs including: o Ethics o Safeguarding o POSH o Information Security o Code of Conduct • Maintain training records and learning dashboards. • Support leadership development and capability-building programs. 8. Employee Relations & Workplace Culture • Serve as a trusted HR partner for employee relations matters. • Support grievance management, disciplinary processes, investigations, and conflict resolution. • Coordinate employee engagement, wellbeing, diversity, equity, inclusion, and recognition initiatives. • Facilitate employee communication and feedback mechanisms. • Promote a positive, inclusive, and values-driven workplace culture. 9. HR Systems, Data Governance & Analytics • Administer HRMS and employee databases. • Ensure integrity, security, confidentiality, and proper maintenance of employee data. • Generate HR dashboards and workforce analytics reports. • Monitor and analyze: o Attrition trends o Recruitment metrics o Diversity data o Workforce costs o Employee engagement indicators • Identify opportunities for automation and process improvement. 10. Vendor & Third-Party Workforce Compliance • Manage relationships with HR service providers, recruitment agencies, insurance providers, training vendors, and background verification vendors. • Monitor vendor compliance and service quality. 11. Budgeting & Financial Coordination • Support preparation and monitoring of annual HR budgets. • Track recruitment, employee benefit, learning and development, and engagement costs. • Support HR inputs for annual operating plans and workforce budgeting. • Coordinate HR-related procurement and vendor payments. 12. Organizational Development & Change Management • Support organizational restructuring, job evaluation, role alignment, and workforce optimization initiatives. • Assist in developing organization structures and staffing models. • Support change management activities associated with growth, transformation, and organizational transitions. • Facilitate employee communication and transition management during organizational change. 13. Risk Management, Ethics & Safeguarding • Support implementation of ethics, safeguarding, whistleblower, and workplace conduct frameworks. • Monitor compliance with organizational policies and mandatory training requirements. • Support investigations involving misconduct, policy violations, and employee complaints. • Maintain records and documentation related to employee conduct matters. • Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, and ethical behavior. 14. Corporate Governance, Board & Regulatory Reporting • Support preparation of HR reports for management, Board, investors, regulatory bodies, auditors, and other stakeholders. • Maintain audit-ready HR documentation and compliance records. • Support HR due diligence exercises, internal reviews, and corporate governance assessments. • Prepare workforce reports, compliance reports, and people metrics for leadership review. • Ensure organizational readiness for donor reviews, governance audits, and regulatory inspections. Qualifications • Master's Degree in Human Resources, Personnel Management, Business Administration, Social Work, or related discipline. • Professional certification in HR or labor law compliance would be an added advantage. Experience • 6–8 years of progressively responsible HR experience. • Experience across HR operations, recruitment, performance management, labor law compliance, and employee relations. • Experience supporting audits, compliance reviews, and HR governance processes. • Experience in a healthcare, consulting, not-for-profit, development sector, or corporate environment preferred. • Experience supporting a new entity setup, organizational transition, or high-growth environment will be an advantage. Key Competencies Functional • HR Operations • Labor Law Compliance • HR Governance • Audit Readiness • Compensation & Benefits • Talent Acquisition • Employee Relations • HR Analytics • HR Systems Behavioral • Integrity & Confidentiality • Attention to Detail • Ownership & Accountability • Stakeholder Management • Problem Solving • Analytical Thinking • Collaboration • Change Agility The Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. Women candidates and candidates from underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged to apply. Interested candidates are requested to share their updated resume along with a cover letter at the following email address : publichealthconsultancy9@gmail.com

description: Associate Director – Finance and Operations New Delhi A Public Health Consulting Organization We are a health systems consulting organization dedicated to strengthening public health outcomes across India. We partner with government agencies, healthcare providers, development organizations, academic institutions, and funding partners to address complex public health challenges through practical, evidence-based solutions. Our work spans health systems strengthening, primary healthcare, digital health, environmental health, mental health, nutrition, and emergency response, with a strong focus on improving the health of women and children. Combining technical expertise with implementation experience, we help partners translate strategy into measurable impact. Operating as a professional consulting organization, we deliver high-quality advisory and implementation support with agility, rigor, and a commitment to sustainable health outcomes for communities across India. ROLE PURPOSE The Associate Director – Finance and Operations (AD) is a strategic member of the executive leadership team and is responsible for the Company's overall financial strategy, stewardship, performance, governance, and risk management. The AD will provide financial leadership to support profitable growth, capital allocation, operational efficiency, business planning, and long-term value creation. The role combines strategic finance leadership with oversight of accounting, financial planning and analysis, treasury, taxation, statutory compliance, internal controls, audit, working capital, commercial finance, and financial risk management. The AD will serve as a trusted advisor to the Managing Director/CEO and Board, translating financial and operational data into actionable business intelligence. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Strategic Finance & Business Leadership • Serve as a key member of the senior leadership team, providing financial insight and challenge to strategic and commercial decisions. • Develop and implement a multi-year finance strategy aligned with business growth, profitability, capital requirements, and shareholder objectives. • Partner with the MD/CEO and business heads on business strategy, expansion plans, pricing, investment decisions, restructuring, and performance improvement initiatives. • Establish financial targets, value drivers, KPIs, and performance dashboards and use them to drive accountability across the organisation. • Evaluate business cases, acquisitions, investments, new products/markets, and major contracts from financial, commercial, tax, and risk perspectives. 2. Financial Management, Accounting & Reporting • Oversee the complete finance and accounting function, including general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, payroll accounting, provisions, reconciliations, and month-end/year-end closing. • Ensure accurate, timely, and decision-useful monthly and management financial reporting to the MD/CEO and Board. • Lead preparation of annual financial statements in accordance with applicable Indian Accounting Standards / Accounting Standards and Companies Act requirements, as applicable. • Ensure integrity of the ERP/accounting systems, chart of accounts, cost centres, financial master data, and management reporting architecture. • Establish robust financial controls, accounting policies, delegation of authority, and close processes. 3. FP&A, Budgeting, Forecasting & Performance Management • Lead the annual operating plan, budgeting, rolling forecast, and long-range financial planning processes. • Develop scenario analyses, sensitivity analyses, cash-flow forecasts, and profitability models to support management decisions. • Monitor actual performance against budget, forecast, and business KPIs; identify variances, root causes, and corrective actions. • Provide commercial finance support for pricing, margins, customer profitability, product economics, cost optimisation, and business unit performance. • Drive a performance-management culture through clear financial targets and periodic business reviews. 4. Treasury, Cash Flow & Working Capital • Own the Company's cash-flow strategy, liquidity planning, banking relationships, and treasury operations. • Optimise working capital through disciplined management of receivables, payables, inventory, advances, and cash conversion cycle. • Oversee bank facilities, borrowing arrangements, guarantees, letters of credit, investments, and financing requirements, subject to Board approvals. • Develop cash-flow forecasts and ensure adequate liquidity for operating and strategic requirements. • Monitor foreign exchange, interest-rate, counterparty, and other financial risks where relevant. 5. Taxation, Statutory Compliance & Corporate Governance • Oversee direct and indirect tax compliance, including GST, income tax, TDS, transfer pricing, ROC, and other applicable statutory requirements. • Ensure timely and accurate statutory filings, tax assessments, notices, and regulatory submissions in coordination with tax advisors and internal teams. • Monitor compliance with the Companies Act, FEMA and other applicable corporate, financial, and regulatory requirements. • Advise management and the Board on significant tax, regulatory, and governance matters and ensure appropriate documentation and approvals. • Maintain a strong compliance culture and proactively identify emerging regulatory risks. 6. Audit, Internal Controls & Risk Management • Lead coordination of statutory, internal, tax, and other relevant audits and ensure timely closure of audit observations. • Strengthen the Company's internal control framework, including financial controls, segregation of duties, approval matrices, and fraud-prevention mechanisms. • Establish and maintain an enterprise financial risk-management framework covering financial, operational, compliance, and commercial risks. • Ensure robust control over financial reporting and maintain audit-ready documentation. • Provide the Board/Audit Committee with transparent reporting on key financial risks, control deficiencies, and remediation plans. 7. Commercial Finance & Cost Optimisation • Partner with commercial and operational teams to improve revenue quality, gross margins, EBITDA, cost efficiency, and return on capital. • Review major customer/vendor contracts, pricing arrangements, commercial terms, and financial commitments. • Identify cost-saving and productivity opportunities without compromising business growth or service quality. • Develop profitability analysis by product, customer, geography, channel, project, or business unit, as relevant. • Support negotiations with customers, suppliers, lenders, investors, and other stakeholders from a financial and commercial perspective. 8. Procurement, Vendor & Contract Financial Oversight • Provide financial governance over procurement and major vendor engagements, ensuring value for money, appropriate approvals, and commercial discipline. • Oversee financial due diligence and risk assessment for significant suppliers and contracts. • Establish appropriate controls over purchase commitments, vendor payments, advances, and contract renewals. • Monitor procurement spend and vendor concentration risks and promote cost-effective sourcing strategies. 9. Technology, Systems & Finance Transformation • Lead the finance transformation agenda, including ERP optimisation, automation, management dashboards, and digital finance processes. • Ensure finance systems provide reliable, timely, and integrated data for management decision-making. • Drive process standardisation, automation, analytics, and continuous improvement across the finance function. • Evaluate and implement appropriate financial technology solutions in line with business needs and control requirements. 10. People Leadership & Team Development • Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing finance organisation with clear roles, KPIs, accountability, and succession plans. • Build strong technical and business partnering capabilities within the finance team. • Promote a culture of integrity, ownership, commercial thinking, continuous improvement, and service excellence. • Ensure appropriate talent, structure, policies, and professional development to support the Company's growth. 11. Board, Investor & Stakeholder Management • Prepare and present financial performance, forecasts, cash-flow, risk, and strategic finance matters to the Board and relevant committees. • Act as a key financial interface with shareholders, investors, lenders, auditors, tax advisors, regulators, insurers, and other external stakeholders. • Support fundraising, debt financing, investor discussions, due diligence, and other strategic transactions, where applicable. • Ensure transparent, timely, and credible financial communication to internal and external stakeholders. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE • Qualified Chartered Accountant (CA); CPA, CFA, or equivalent qualification is an asset. • Minimum 15 years of progressive finance experience, including significant experience in a senior finance leadership / AD / Finance Director role in a private-sector, commercial, or for-profit environment. • Strong experience in financial strategy, FP&A, accounting, taxation, treasury, working capital, internal controls, audit, and business performance management. • Demonstrated experience partnering with CEOs, business heads, and Boards on strategic and commercial decisions. • Proven track record of improving profitability, cash generation, cost efficiency, controls, and financial discipline. • Experience with ERP systems and advanced financial reporting, analytics, and business intelligence tools. • Experience in managing banking relationships, debt/equity financing, due diligence, or corporate transactions is desirable. • Strong knowledge of Indian corporate, taxation, Companies Act, GST, FEMA, and other applicable regulatory requirements. KEY COMPETENCIES • Strategic financial acumen with the ability to translate financial data into business intelligence and actionable decisions. • Strong commercial orientation with a clear focus on profitability, cash flow, return on capital, and shareholder value. • Excellent knowledge of accounting, FP&A, taxation, treasury, internal controls, and financial risk management. • High integrity, ethical leadership, sound judgement, and strong corporate governance orientation. • Analytical rigour, attention to detail, and ability to manage complexity and ambiguity under pressure. • Strong communication, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills, with credibility at Board and executive levels. • Ability to challenge constructively while partnering effectively with commercial and operational leaders. • Strong people leadership, coaching, team development, and succession-planning capabilities. • Ability to lead finance transformation, automation, and data-driven decision-making in a growing organisation. SUCCESS MEASURES • Timely and accurate financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, and management information. • Strong working-capital performance and disciplined capital allocation. • Effective statutory compliance, audit outcomes, and internal control environment. • Reduction of controllable costs and improvement in finance process efficiency. • Quality and timeliness of Board and management decision support. • Development of a high-performing, scalable, and business-oriented finance function. The Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. Women candidates and candidates from underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged to apply. Interested candidates are requested to share their updated resume along with a cover letter at the following email address publichealthconsultancy9@gmail.com

description: Job Description Senior Manager – Resource Mobilization & Donor Management About Us Normal 0 false false false false EN-IN X-NONE X-NONE /* Style Definitions */ table.MsoNormalTable {mso-style-name:"Table Normal"; mso-tstyle-rowband-size:0; mso-tstyle-colband-size:0; mso-style-noshow:yes; mso-style-priority:99; mso-style-parent:""; mso-padding-alt:0cm 5.4pt 0cm 5.4pt; mso-para-margin-top:0cm; mso-para-margin-right:0cm; mso-para-margin-bottom:8.0pt; mso-para-margin-left:0cm; line-height:115%; mso-pagination:widow-orphan; font-size:12.0pt; font-family:"Aptos",sans-serif; mso-ascii-font-family:Aptos; mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-hansi-font-family:Aptos; mso-hansi-theme-font:minor-latin; mso-font-kerning:1.0pt; mso-ligatures:standardcontextual; mso-fareast-language:EN-US;} Digital Green India is a social impact organization helping farmers harness technology and data to build resilient and prosperous communities. Founded in 2008 out of Microsoft Research Lab, it began with a video-based approach that transformed how agricultural advisory reached rural communities. Over the years, the organization has partnered with governments, the private sector, and civil society to scale digital tools and AI-driven platforms across India. To date, Digital Green, in India, has reached 6.5 million smallholder farmers (50% women), trained more than 100,000 frontline workers (52% women), and supported hundreds of farmer groups in producing and sharing localized videos in 26 languages. Building on 18 years of experience, it is now advancing a farmer-responsive, AI-enabled model of extension. In 2024, Digital Green launched FarmerChat, an open-source, AI-powered solution designed to strengthen public systems and deliver climate-smart, hyperlocal guidance in farmers’ own languages. In India, the tool has reached close to 1 million users (45% women), who have asked millions of queries. By continuously innovating and expanding digital solutions, we remain committed to driving meaningful change. Our team is passionate about transformative change, fostering resilience, and making a tangible impact. Joining Digital Green India means joining a team of forward-thinking leaders in technology-driven development and social impact in India. If you’re a visionary who shares our values and seeks to drive impactful partnerships for the greater good, we invite you to join our mission. www.digitalgreentrust.org About the Role Senior Manager – Resource Mobilization & Donor Partnerships plays a central role in advancing the organization's fundraising strategy by developing high-quality funding opportunities and nurturing donor relationships. The role works closely with the Head of Resource Mobilization, CEO, technical teams, finance, and program teams to translate organizational priorities into compelling concepts, proposals, and donor engagement strategies. The role is responsible for managing the end-to-end development of funding proposals, coordinating donor requirements throughout the fundraising lifecycle, and ensuring continuity in relationships with existing donors. The position contributes to fundraising strategy through research, donor engagement support, and cross-functional coordination while ensuring that donor expectations are translated into strong, implementable project designs. Why Join Digital Green Work at the intersection of AI and social impact — helping take FarmerChat, an AI-powered advisory, to the last mile, where it reaches hundreds of thousands of farmers and extension workers in their own languages, by voice, text and image. Be part of a genuinely farmer-first organization, where technology is designed around the realities of low-literacy, low-connectivity rural India, and success is measured by what reaches and works for the farmer. Direct exposure to work alongside the senior leadership team on the organization's most strategic priorities. Opportunity to gain a 360° view of building and scaling programmes through partnerships. Be associated with a fast-growing, mission-driven organization with high ownership and low bureaucracy. Be part of a culture that values initiative, learning, and impact. Key Responsibilities 1. Proposal & Concept Development Lead the development of high-quality concept notes, proposals, presentations, and funding applications that align donor priorities with organizational strategy. Coordinate with program, technical, MEL, product, and finance teams to design interventions that are technically robust, financially viable, and operationally feasible. Ensure proposals clearly articulate outcomes, impact pathways, implementation approaches, and value propositions for prospective donors. Continuously improve proposal quality by incorporating learning from previous submissions, donor feedback, and sector trends. 2. Resource Mobilization Conduct donor mapping, opportunity assessment, and connect with potential donors. Participate in fundraising conversations with prospective partners. Track fundraising opportunities and support timely follow-up actions to advance partnership discussions. 3. Donor Relationship Management Maintain regular engagement with existing donor partners assigned to the role to ensure continuity in relationship management. Coordinate donor requests, respond to routine communication, and facilitate timely resolution of queries during proposal development and implementation. Build trusted relationships by proactively understanding donor priorities and identifying opportunities for deeper engagement. 4. Cross-functional Coordination & Project Design Coordinate across program, finance, product, and technical teams to gather inputs required for proposals and donor deliverables. Ensure budgets, implementation plans, and technical narratives remain aligned throughout proposal development. Support internal reviews and quality assurance processes prior to proposal submission. 5. Knowledge Management & Strategic Support Maintain proposal repositories, donor intelligence, and fundraising documentation. Capture learning from successful and unsuccessful proposals to strengthen future fundraising efforts. Support strategic initiatives undertaken by the Resource Mobilization team as required. Educational Qualifications & Experience: Relevant degree in Development Studies, Public Policy, Agriculture, Rural Management, Business Administration, or related field. 8-12 years of experience in fundraising, proposal development, partnerships, or donor management. Demonstrated experience writing successful grant proposals for CSR, foundations, bilateral, or multilateral donors. Strong project design and logical framework development skills. Experience developing project budgets in collaboration with finance teams. Excellent stakeholder management and relationship-building skills. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to coordinate across multiple teams and manage competing deadlines. High proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and collaborative documentation tools. Experience in agriculture, livelihoods, digital development, or climate resilience is preferred. Familiarity with donor compliance requirements and grant lifecycle management. Experience working with technology-enabled development programs. Required Skills & Competencies: Strategic thinking and decision-making Collaboration, communication, and influencing skills Strong ownership and accountability Excellent attention to detail Strong problem-solving and analytical skills Relationship management and stakeholder engagement Adaptability and ability to work in a changing environment How to Apply Position Title: Senior Manager – Resource Mobilization and Donor Management Duration: Two Years Location: New Delhi Reports To: Head, Resource Mobilization and Donor Management Apply by sending your resume or LinkedIn profile to ashokkumar@digitalgreentrust.org with the subject line: "Application for Sr. Manager, RMDM". We also welcome referrals from your network. Digital Green is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and particularly encourage women to apply.

description: NEEDS – Vacancy Announcement Position: Officer Grade – Product Innovation & Design Location: Deoghar, Jharkhand Qualification: B.E./B.Tech. in Civil Engineering or equivalent Salary: Negotiable, based on demonstrated competency and experience Nature of Position: Technical, Innovation & Design About the Position NEEDS is looking for a technically competent and creatively oriented Officer – Product Innovation & Design to strengthen its product development and artisan-support ecosystem. We are made up of government and non-government agencies, charities, donors and funders, professional groups, patient groups and civil society organisations. We bring together clinicians, managers, policy makers, front-line workers and implementers, scientists, patients and survivors, advocates and civil society. The Union’s Vision: A healthier world for all, free of tuberculosis and lung disease The Union’s Mission: The Union strives to end suffering due to tuberculosis and lung disease by advancing better prevention and care. We seek to achieve this by the generation, dissemination and implementation of knowledge into policy and practice. We aim to ensure that no-one is left behind, people are treated equally and we have a focus on vulnerable and marginalised populations and communities. The Union’s Values: • Quality: we deliver our services and products to the highest possible standards. • Transparency: we are open and direct in our dealings. • Accountability: we are responsible stewards of resources, deliver on our commitments, and are accountable to our stakeholders. • Respect: we recognise people’s intrinsic value and have due regard for the welfare, beliefs, perceptions, customs and cultural heritage of those we deal with. • Independence: we seek to pursue our mission free from interference by conflicts of interest. About the Project: In India, unified and collective action is crucial in the fight against TB. With millions affected annually, a collaborative approach that leverages diverse expertise is essential. The Union proposes to work in close collaboration with Central TB Division, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, GoI and NTEP State and district program managers in the State of Chhattisgarh and Punjab for a period of eleven months through a donor funded project. The project proposes to pilot innovations for improving access to facility-based and home-based Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment (TPT) services within private health facilities, with a focus on multi-specialty/corporate hospitals, chemists and laboratories. The scope involves implementing and evaluating integrated service delivery models to improve TB prevention and treatment completion outcomes. The expected outcome is to develop a sustainable, costed system that generates increased demand for TPT and achieves a high treatment completion rate. The project will build coordination system between NTEP and private health facilities for initial engagement, capacity building, and streamlining service delivery. The intervention will include the functioning of the concept of "TPT Centres" on a pilot basis within selected multi-specialty/corporate hospitals or jointly the private hospital & laboratories to offer a comprehensive TPT service for the close contacts of the TB patients notified in the private sector, deploying a standardized TPT cascade, including screening, initiation, and follow-up. The staff will activate a secure supply chain mechanism to distribute TPT to the TPT Centres/ Chemists and doorstep delivery of NTEP-provided, free TPT medications to beneficiaries and conduct comprehensive upskilling and capacity-building through orientation sessions for diverse private healthcare providers, addressing knowledge gaps on TPT eligibility, assessment, and scientific updates. The goal of the proposed project is to achieve at least 80% screening and testing coverage of eligible Household Contacts (HHCs) of people with TB, notified from the private sector and more than 90% treatment completion rate among those who are initiated on TPT. household contacts, their TPT status and eligibility for TPT after thorough assessment. • Take consent for testing of TPT – among household contacts. • Mobilise household contacts to nearest collection centres and Chest X-ray (CXR) facilities if needed. • Communicate with laboratory representative for collecting and processing the samples • Record and report the investigation results. • Communicate the investigation results to household contacts and clarify their doubts. • Follow up with household contacts for consultation with the private doctor • Facilitate the TPT initiation among eligible household contacts • Ensure that all diagnosed TB patients are placed on anti-TB treatment • Following up with household contacts up to treatment completion • Record and report the three/ six months follow-up reports. • Build systems for sustaining contact follow up models by engaging ASHA workers, community volunteers etc • Provide a monthly report to the DTO and the District PPM Lead • Participate in monthly meetings of NTEP and update the NTEP on the achievements, challenges and solutions to field difficulties. • Provide all necessary information related to the project to SPMU/NPMU as and when required. • Escalate issues to District PPM Leads as and when required • Maintain all recording and reporting formats as per project requirements. description: Just Rights for Children (JRC) | Global Head of Communications Senior Leadership | Global Narrative, Brand, Advocacy and Public Affairs About Just Rights for Children Just Rights for Children (JRC) is a network of over 300 organisations working to prevent violence against children, with a particular focus on rape, sexual abuse and exploitation. Operating across India, Nepal, Kenya, UK and the United States, JRC is building a scalable, ecosystem-level response through legal intervention, community engagement and the rule of law. Our goal is to eliminate impunity for all forms of child sexual abuse and exploitation by reaching a tipping point of legal action and deterrence. As JRC expands internationally, we are seeking a senior communications leader to build its global voice, reputation and influence. About The Role The Global Head of Communications will define and lead JRC’s global communications strategy, positioning the network as a leading global voice on justice, accountability and protection for children. This is a senior leadership mandate focused on narrative, influence, reputation and institutional positioning . The role will work closely with JRC’s leadership to ensure that its legal interventions, grassroots impact and global advocacy priorities shape policy, public discourse and global action. Strategic Mandate Define and own JRC’s global narrative, positioning and brand architecture. Build JRC’s international profile across governments, multilateral institutions, media, civil society and global policy platforms. Translate complex legal, policy and programme work into clear, compelling narratives with global relevance. Lead strategic communications around major campaigns, legal interventions, judgments, policy developments and international advocacy moments. Build a proactive global media and thought leadership strategy. Position JRC’s leadership and experts as influential voices in international debates on violence against children, justice and accountability. Set the strategic direction for digital and social media as tools for advocacy, mobilisation and reputation. Advise senior leadership on public affairs, stakeholder perception, reputation and communications risk. Build and lead a high-performing communications function across priority geographies. Establish strong global standards for messaging, brand, spokesperson engagement and communications governance. What Success Looks Like JRC is recognised internationally as a credible and influential voice on ending violence against children through the rule of law. Policymakers, media, jurists and global institutions actively seek JRC’s perspective and evidence. JRC has a clear, distinctive and consistent global identity across markets and platforms. Its communications function anticipates and shapes conversations rather than simply responding to them. Communications strengthens JRC’s ability to influence policy, mobilise action and advance accountability for crimes against children. Candidate Profile The successful candidate will bring: Senior-level experience in global communications, advocacy, public affairs or institutional brand strategy. Strong international media, policy and stakeholder experience. Sophisticated judgment in politically and reputationally sensitive environments. A track record of shaping organisational narratives and building institutional influence. Experience working across governments, multilaterals, civil society and other high-level stakeholders. Proven ability to lead teams and communications functions across countries and cultures. Exceptional ability to translate complex issues into clear, authoritative and compelling communications. Strong alignment with JRC’s mission and its belief in the rule of law as a means to prevent violence, end impunity and protect children. Reporting and Scope The Global Head of Communications will report to JRC’s senior leadership and carry a global mandate across existing and emerging markets. The role will combine strategic counsel, global positioning and team leadership, with responsibility for building the communications capability required for JRC’s next phase of international growth. Educational Qualification : Graduate/Master's Degree in Communications/ Journalism/ Mass Communication/Public Relations /Marketing, International Relations/Development Studies/Public Policy or a related field. Experience: 15+ years of experience Salary: Salary will be offered commensurate with qualifications, experience and prevailing organisational norms. title: RFP - For A Digital Campaign On Positive Experiences Of Care

description: RFP FOR A DIGITAL CAMPAIGN ON POSITIVE EXPERIENCES OF CARE Background What makes a maternity care experience a positive one? Beyond clinical outcomes, women value being treated with dignity, listened to, informed, supported and responded to with care throughout pregnancy, childbirth and the postnatal period. Yet these dimensions of maternity care are often less visible and less consistently understood than clinical quality. Centre for Catalyzing Change (C3) has been working in India to advance Respectful Maternity Care (RMC) and promote a woman-centred approach to maternity care, where quality is understood not only in terms of clinical outcomes, but also in terms of how women experience their care. As part of its ongoing work, C3 has undertaken a large-scale research initiative to understand women's positive and respectful experiences of pregnancy, childbirth and postnatal care . The research captures what women value in their interactions with healthcare providers and institutions and provides important insights into what can make maternity care more respectful, responsive and woman centred. C3 is now seeking a creative and experienced Design and Digital Marketing Agency to conceptualize, design and implement a high-impact digital campaign t hat brings these findings to life and sparks a wider conversation about what good maternity care looks and feels like. Campaign Vision and Focus The larger vision of this initiative is to strengthen the understanding of respectful and compassionate maternity care as an integral part of quality healthcare, particularly within the private healthcare sector. The campaign, expected to run for approximately 2–3 months, should focus on: Making positive experiences of maternity care visible, demonstrating that dignity, communication, responsiveness, support and respect are integral to quality care and the patient experience. Bringing women's voices and research findings into the public conversation, translating evidence on what women value in maternity care into compelling and accessible digital content. Creating visibility and engagement around C3's digital RMC Compendium of Best practices, highlighting practical, evidence-informed approaches that healthcare institutions can adopt to strengthen experiences of care. Encouraging healthcare professionals and institutions to take action and publicly demonstrate their commitment to better maternity care, moving from awareness to tangible changes in how women experience care. Scope of Work The selected agency will be responsible for developing and executing an innovative and audience-focused digital campaign on Respectful Maternity Care. 1. Campaign Concept and Creative Strategy Conceptualize and develop a compelling, public-facing campaign on RMC. Develop the overall campaign identity, creative concept, messaging framework and visual language. Create a content and performance marketing strategy across different digital platforms and audiences. 2. Campaign Creative Assets and Templates. Develop a set of strong, adaptable master creative formats that can be used across the campaign. These may include: Static social media ad template Short-form video/reel concepts and visual template Copy, scripts, headlines, calls-to-action and messaging adaptations for different campaign themes and audiences. Adaptable design templates that allow the campaign to incorporate research findings, women's experiences, expert voices and other campaign content. The agency should recommend the most effective mix and volume of creative formats based on the proposed campaign strategy. 3. Digital RMC Compendium. C3 has already developed a Compendium on Positive Experience of Care. The selected agency will transform the existing content into a visually compelling and highly engaging digital product, such as an interactive PDF, or any other suitable format. 4. Design RMC Webpage Conceptualize and design an engaging, appealing webpage based on the Digital RMC Compendium. Ensure the webpage is visually compelling, intuitive, mobile-responsive and aligned with the overall campaign identity. Coding and development will be taken care of by C3 5. 360 degree VR Hospital Conceptualize and develop a simple but engaging 360° virtual hospital/healthcare experience that allows users to observe and experience what a high-quality, patient-centred hospital environment looks like in practice. The experience should be accessible through VR headsets and 360° video platforms such as YouTube. The agency should recommend an approach that is creative, technically feasible and appropriate to the available budget. 5. Media Strategy and Campaign Execution Develop and implement a promotional strategy (including paid media) to maximize campaign visibility and public endorsement of the compendium. Recommend the most appropriate platforms, channels, and media mix based on the campaign objectives and audiences. Achieve a minimum cumulative campaign reach of 60 lakh people (6 million) during the campaign period. Recommend additional campaign performance indicators that can realistically be achieved within the available budget, such as engagement, campaign webpage traffic, Compendium downloads, digital endorsements or other relevant actions. Requirements for the Agency. The agency should demonstrate: A strong track record of conceptualizing and executing impactful digital and social media campaigns across India. The ability to develop a comprehensive campaign strategy and translate complex social or health issues into simple, compelling and engaging communication. A demonstrated ability to think beyond conventional social media campaigns and propose innovative, audience-centred approaches and digital experiences. Strong capabilities in creative strategy, design, video production, digital content development and interactive experiences. Experience in developing interactive digital products and immersive experiences. Experience with web-based interactive platforms and/or virtual reality solutions will be an advantage. Demonstrated experience in achieving measurable campaign outcomes, including large-scale reach, engagement and audience growth. Target Audiences. Primary Audiences Private hospitals and healthcare institutions. Hospital leadership, administrators and healthcare decision-makers involved in healthcare management, quality of care and patient experience Healthcare providers and senior clinical professionals. Professional medical and healthcare bodies, associations and networks. Secondary Audience The wider public. Application Process Interested agencies are requested to submit a PowerPoint presentation showcasing relevant work and experience. The presentation should include: An overview of the agency and its relevant experience Examples of major media and social media campaigns designed and implemented Communication and media strategy adopted Platforms and mediums leveraged Types of content and creative assets developed Experience relevant to interactive digital products and/or immersive experiences, if available Examples of campaigns where measurable reach or performance targets were achieved. Shortlisted agencies will be invited for a detailed briefing and will be required to present their proposed approach and pitch to the C3 team. The final agency will be selected based on the overall quality of its experience, creative and strategic capabilities, demonstrated campaign impact, proposed approach and presentation to the selection committee. Budget: Up to Rs 15 lakh, inclusive of all costs related to strategy, creative development, design, digital development, campaign execution, and performance marketing. Last date for submission: September 8, 2026. Please submit the PowerPoint presentation to procurement@c3india.org with the subject line: Digital Campaign on Positive Experiences of Care

description: Request for Proposal (RFP) Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (India) is hiring a consulting agency to conduct an impact study in one of its project region Madhya Pradesh. The proposed Impact study will be conducted for the project titled “ Impact Assessment of Livestock (Poultry & Goatry) Programme of AKRSP(I) in Madhya Pradesh” Objective of this study is to understand the changes attributable to livestock interventions in productivity, mortality, herd/flock size, feeding, animal health, income, women's economic participation and livelihood resilience, and to compare outcomes between intervention and non-intervention areas. Project Background Livestock is an important component of rural livelihoods, particularly for small and marginal farmers and households with limited land and other productive resources. It provides regular income, supports household resilience and acts as an important source of livelihood diversification. AKRSP(I) has been working with rural communities on livestock development, particularly goat rearing, poultry and dairy, through interventions aimed at improving productivity, reducing mortality, strengthening animal health and feeding practices, improving access to services and finance, and enhancing market opportunities. Scope of studies To assess the impact, effectiveness and sustainability of AKRSP(I)'s livestock interventions on livestock productivity, mortality, household income, women's economic participation and livelihood resilience, with a comparative assessment of programme and non-programme areas. Specific Objectives of the study will: Assess changes in livestock ownership, herd/flock size and composition among participating households. Measure changes in livestock mortality and identify the contribution of programme interventions to mortality reduction. Assess changes in feeding, housing, breeding, vaccination, deworming and other livestock-management practices. Assess changes in livestock productivity and reproductive performance. Assess the economic impact of livestock interventions on household income, expenditure, profitability and returns. Assess the contribution of livestock to household livelihood diversification and risk mitigation. Assess the effectiveness and sustainability of Pashu Sakhi services and their contribution to preventive animal healthcare. Assess the adoption and impact of feed-related interventions, including feed blocks and Azolla, where applicable. Assess the role of financial services, government schemes and market linkages in strengthening livestock-based livelihoods. Assess the participation and economic empowerment of women through livestock activities. Compare livestock outcomes between AKRSP(I) working and non-working villages/areas. Identify factors influencing adoption, productivity, income and sustainability of livestock interventions. Identify key lessons, gaps and opportunities for strengthening and scaling livestock interventions. Role of Youths in Livestock based enterprise interventions. Assess the aspirations, capacities, skills, resources and constraints of potential entrepreneurs, particularly women and youth. It reflects TCLP’s current understanding of the Head of Leadership Development role and is expected to evolve through practice, reflection, and dialogue. Role Summary The Head of Leadership Development is responsible for the conceptual leadership, design, implementation, and growth of TCLP’s Leadership Development Department across two core tracks: ? Student Leadership Development (ages 13–18) ? Youth & Community Leadership Development (ages 18+) This role carries organisation-wide responsibility for building leadership as community ownership, not as individual advancement. The position exists to ensure that TCLP’s libraries are run with, by, and for the community, and that leadership development remains deeply rooted in politics that are against class exploitation, and caste oppression and foster feminist, democratic, and justice-oriented pedagogy. The Head of Leadership Development stewards a long-term leadership pipeline—from student leaders to youth leaders, community organisers, librarians, TCLP Leadership Council members and library-movement activists—ensuring coherence across age groups, roles, and political purpose. This role is about deepening, systematising, and sustaining leadership work that already exists within TCLP. Purpose of the Role ? To transfer ownership of libraries to the community through structured, sustained leadership development. ? To develop leaders who think critically, act collectively, and organise communities around the Right to Read and broader democratic rights. ? To ensure that leadership development at TCLP is pedagogically rigorous, politically grounded, and operationally integrated with librarianship and organising. ? To strengthen systems that allow leadership development to be scalable, accountable, and sustainable without dilution of values. Departmental Scope The Leadership Development Department includes two interlinked leadership formations: ? Student Leaders (13–18) and Community Organiser Trainees, ie interns (paid, short-term) ? Youth Leaders and Community Organisers (18–25) The Head of Leadership Development holds overall responsibility for coherence, quality, mentorship structures, curriculum alignment, evaluation, and progression pathways across both groups. Key Responsibilities 1. Strategic Leadership & Vision ? Articulate and steward a shared vision of leadership across student and adult tracks, grounded in: ? Community ownership ? Opposition to class exploitation ? Anti-caste and anti-discrimination politics ? Constitutional values ? Libraries as democratic institutions ? Translate TCLP’s philosophical commitments (justice, love, trust, solidarity, community ownership) into concrete leadership practices. ? Ensure leadership development remains central to TCLP’s organisational strategy, not a parallel or add-on program. ? Do this work in close collaboration with librarians, organisers, and senior leadership, recognising leadership development as shared work. 2. Student Leadership Development (Ages 13–18) ? Provide overall leadership for the Student Leadership Program across all TCLP branches. Oversee one Librarian in each branch who is responsible for the SL Program. ? Advice Librarians responsible for SL on : ? Recruitment and nomination processes ? Open training and formal training structures ? Induction ceremonies and annual cycles ? Ensure student leadership curriculum remains: ? Age-appropriate ? Experiential and dialogical ? Integrated with daily library work (circulation, read-alouds, mobilisation, digital library, data, technology). ? Support librarians in their role as mentors and co-educators, not supervisors. ? Ensure parental engagement, consent, and trust-building remain integral to the program. ? Safeguard student leaders’ learning, dignity, safety, and political development. Final responsibility for child safety, safeguarding, and institutional risk remains with the organisation as a whole; the Head of Leadership Development works in partnership with librarians and senior leadership on these matters. 3. Youth & Community Leadership Development (Ages 18+) ? Provide strategic oversight for TCLP’s Youth Leadership and Community Organising track, including externally funded projects (e.g., Azim Premji Foundation). ? Work closely with Project Leads, Curriculum Coordinator, and Community Organisers to: ? Design and deliver training-of-trainers (ToT) modules ? Ensure coherence across quarterly trainings, weekly reading circles, and social action campaigns ? Ensure youth leadership development remains rooted in: ? Issue-based organising ? Praxis (action–reflection–action) ? Reading, dialogue, and critical inquiry ? Support the progression of youth leaders into: ? Community organisers ? Librarians ? Library movement activists ? Engage with funder-linked leadership programs in ways that protect TCLP’s political clarity, pedagogical autonomy, and long-term vision. 4. Curriculum, Pedagogy & Praxis ? Hold responsibility for pedagogical integrity of leadership development across ages. ? Ensure consistent application of: ? Critical pedagogy ? Dialogical methods ? Experiential learning ? Socio-constructivist approaches ? Oversee the Curriculum Coordinator in their work to: ? Develop, refine, and document leadership curricula ? Create training manuals and internal resources for long-term sustainability ? Ensure that everyday library practices (welcoming, circulation, cataloguing, read-alouds, mobilisation) are explicitly connected to: ? Power ? Access ? Knowledge ? Justice ? Embed action–reflection–action cycles across all leadership activities. 5. Organisational Integration & Democratic Governance ? Ensure leadership development is deeply integrated with: ? Branch Libraries ? Local area communities ? Fundraising and Finance Department through overseeing reporting ? Digital library (Duniya Sabki) ? Safety and child-protection systems ? Mobilisation and advocacy beyond the local area when appropriate for issues affecting the local community ? Support democratic participation of member leaders in: ? Leadership Council ? Committees and organisational decision-making in TCLP This role supports democratic processes but does not replace or contradict collective decision-making structures such as the Leadership Council, Trustees, or Steering Committee. 6. Mentorship, Team Development & Care ? Mentor Project Leads, Community Organisers, librarians, and senior youth leaders. ? Build a culture of care, accountability, and collective responsibility within the department. ? Support leaders through: ? Skill building in aspects of leadership ? Sharpening political analysis particularly in class, caste and gender analysis, ? Providing opportunities to take initiative, exercise leadership and experience the power of building the organisation ? Teaching reflection and developing ? Conflict resolution, Burnout prevention ? Ensure leadership development does not replicate hierarchies it seeks to dismantle. 7. Documentation, Evaluation & Reporting ? Oversee systems for: ? Tracking participation and progression ? Qualitative documentation of learning and transformation ? Reflective evaluation ? Metrics as required by funders and as needed for internal evaluation by TCLP ? Contribute to internal reports, funder reports, and organisational learning documents. ? Ensure documentation reflects TCLP’s values and language, not just compliance requirements. ? Emphasis is placed on learning-oriented documentation that supports reflection, course correction, and institutional memory. Position Ethos The Head of Leadership Development is a custodian of TCLP’s future—responsible for ensuring that leadership remains collective, rooted, and accountable to the communities whose right to read and think TCLP exists to uphold. description: INTERNATIONAL MAIZE AND WHEAT IMPROVEMENT CENTRE (CIMMYT INDIA) REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) – Date Extension till Aug 28, 2026 [RFQ: 2026/08/01] 12 th August 2026 Subject: Invitation to Submit Proposal – Assessing the Potential of digital Aflatoxin Risk Scoring for fintech, and Market Systems Dear Sir/Madam, CIMMYT India invites your company to participate in a competitive selection process for the provision of a brief description of goods and services in accordance with the technical specifications and requirements established by the Procurement Unit. Annex I Terms of Reference (ToR) Assessing the Potential of digital Aflatoxin Risk Scoring for fintech, and Market Systems Background The International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT) is a cutting-edge, non-profit international organization committed to addressing tomorrow’s challenges today. As a core CGIAR Research Center and part of a global research partnership working toward a food-secure future, CIMMYT is dedicated to reducing poverty, enhancing food and nutrition security, and improving the sustainable management of natural resources. Smallholder farmers in many low- and middle-income countries continue to face weak incentives to invest in improved grain storage and quality management. Emerging business models have demonstrated the potential to address these constraints by integrating AI-based grain quality assessment, digital warehouse receipt systems, grain-backed financing (fintech), and digital trading platforms. Food safety—particularly contamination by aflatoxins and other mycotoxins—remains a major constraint to market competitiveness, export opportunities, and public health. Conventional laboratory testing provides definitive evidence of contamination but is costly and cannot be applied practically to every grain lot. Recent advances in artificial intelligence offer an opportunity to complement laboratory testing by combining operational data collected throughout the grain value chainand other relevant variables—to generate probabilistic mycotoxin risk scores for individual grain lots. CIMMYT is seeking qualified agri-tech companies in India to undertake a 3 months study to develop and validate a replicable Digital Grain Quality Intelligence framework. The study will explore how AI-based grain quality assessment and probabilistic mycotoxin risk prediction can be integrated with digital warehouse receipt systems, grain-backed financing (fintech), and digital trading platforms to strengthen grain quality management and enable quality-based market incentives. The framework should identify the technical, operational, and institutional components required for implementation and provide guidance for adaptation across different country contexts. Objective: The selected company will be responsible for achieving the following objectives: 1) Assess the feasibility of developing an AI-enabled Digital Grain Quality Intelligence framework for estimating probabilistic mycotoxin risk scores 2) Explain how Digital Grain Quality Intelligence, including mycotoxin risk scores, could be integrated into digital warehouse receipt systems, grain-backed financing, grain grading, procurement decisions, and digital market platforms to strengthen incentives for grain quality management and quality-based price differentiation. 3) Develop a replicable implementation framework that outlines the technical, data, operational, and institutional requirements for adapting AI-enabled Digital Grain Quality Intelligence across maize value chains in different country contexts, with an initial focus on Mexico. Scope of work: The selected company will undertake a study to develop a replicable framework for AI-enabled Digital Grain Quality Intelligence that estimates probabilistic food safety risk scores for maize grain lots and assesses its potential integration into digital grain banking, financing, and market systems. The work will include the following tasks. Design and development Task 1: Development of a Digital Food Safety Risk Scoring Framework The company will assess the feasibility of developing an AI-enabled framework for estimating probabilistic mycotoxin risk scores at the grain-lot level. Develop a Digital Food Safety Risk Scoring Framework that integrates visible grain quality indicators (e.g., discoloration, insect damage), non-visible indicators (e.g., storage conditions, weather,), and AI-based probabilistic risk assessment for different end-use markets. Develop a validation framework using laboratory mycotoxin analyses and digital certificate acceptance/rejection data to calibrate and assess the technical performance and reliability of the probabilistic risk scores. Task 2. Integration with Digital Finance and Market Systems Evaluate opportunities for integration of probabilistic food safety risk scores into digital warehouse receipt systems, warehouse receipt financing, procurement, grain grading, and quality-based market pricing. Develop a replicable implementation framework outlining the technical, institutional, and operational requirements for adapting AI-enabled Digital Food Safety Risk Scoring across maize value chains, with an initial focus on Mexico. Deliverables and time line The selected company shall deliver: Inception Report including methodology, workplan 7 th of September Framework for probabilistic mycotoxin risk scoring and its’ integration of probabilistic food safety risk scores into digital warehouse receipt systems, warehouse receipt financing, procurement, grain grading, and quality-based market pricing. 30 October Final report including scalable implementation guidelines and recommendations for country adaptation 30 November

description: Publish date – 21 August 2026 Position Code : PHFI-CNST-2675 Position Title : Consultant - Senior Research Fellow (Quantitative) No. of Positions : 1 Location : Bangalore Duration of Position : 01 Year or co-terminus with the project, whichever is earlier Brief on the Organization: The Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) is working towards building a healthier India. It is helping to address the limited institutional and systems capacity in India by strengthening education and training, advancing research and technology and facilitating policy and practice in the area of Public Health. PHFI is headquartered in New Delhi with national presence through its constituent units of regional Indian Institutes of Public Health (IIPHs) and Centers of Applied Research in core public health themes. The Foundation, established in 2006 as a public private initiative, is governed by an independent board comprising of senior government officials, eminent Indian and International academic and leaders, civil society representatives and corporate leaders. For more information, please visit the website www.phfi.org . Project Brief: The Public health foundation of India is implementing a project “ Meeting the Challenge of Urban PHC Systems in India - A Learning Sites Approach”. This research project is funded by University college of London and will be carried out in close collaboration with PHFI and IIT Kanpur across three learning sites: Bhubaneswar, Bengaluru, and Kanpur. The proposed multi-centric research aims to systematically examine the challenges and gaps in urban primary healthcare systems. The study will employ rigorous quantitative and qualitative research methods, including primary data collection, secondary data review, and comprehensive stakeholder consultations. About National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) The National Capital Region Planning Board is statutory body constituted under the act of Parliament, under Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The growth of population of Delhi has contributed to increasing congestion and shortages of civic amenities. Hence, this Board was started with the purpose to address problems of land, housing, transportation and management of essential infrastructure like water supply and sewerage that have become more acute. NCRPB is also implementing two central sector schemes of the Government of India in National Capital Region (NCR) i.e. Naya Safar Yojana Scheme, Swach Pawan Neel Gagan Swasth NCR (SPNG- NCR). Urban and Regional Planning • Lead the preparation, review, and quality assurance of functional plans, sub-regional plans, and other statutory or non-statutory planning documents. • Advise on the operationalisation of plan policies, including preparation of guidance notes, etc. • Conduct conformity reviews of sub-regional plans, master/ development plans, etc. prepared by State Town Planning Departments, UDAs, and ULBs as per the regional plan. • Provide technical advisory inputs on land use planning, urban form, density, transit-oriented development (TOD), and town planning schemes, etc. Transportation and Mobility Planning • Provide technical advisory inputs on urban transport planning including mass transit (metro, RRTS, BRT, bus systems), non-motorised transport, freight and logistics, and mobility integration. • Review transport demand assessments, comprehensive mobility plans (CMPs), and station-area development plans for transit corridors. • Advise on multi-modal integration, last-mile connectivity, and TOD implementation along major transit corridors. • Prepare cross-jurisdictional transport coordination notes for use in inter-state or inter-agency forums.
