description: JOB DESCRIPTION Suraksha Coordinator – Jhargram About Mukti Mukti is a development organisation dedicated to advancing the well-being, education and empowerment of children, young people and underserved communities. Through its work with schools and communities, Mukti strives to foster safe, inclusive and enabling environments where children can learn, grow and realise their potential. Safeguarding is integral to Mukti’s organisational ethos. The organisation has established robust Child Safeguarding and POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Policies and is committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety, dignity, inclusion, professional integrity and accountability across all its programmes and engagements. About Suraksha Songlap Suraksha Songlap is a school-based initiative designed to strengthen child safety, gender sensitivity, awareness and safeguarding practices among adolescents, teachers, facilitators and the wider school community. The programme is being implemented in three project schools in Jhargram: Ranarani, Banpukhuria and Manikpara. Position Designation: Suraksha Coordinator Location: Jhargram, West Bengal Project: Suraksha Songlap Reporting to: Suraksha Programme Manager Remuneration: 12,000 per month + TA on actual basis Travel: Frequent travel between the three project schools will be an integral part of the role. Key Purpose of the Role: The Suraksha Coordinator will be responsible for the effective field-level implementation, coordination, monitoring and documentation of the Suraksha Songlap programme across the three project schools. The Coordinator will work under the continuous guidance and supervision of the Suraksha Programme Manager, receive appropriate programme-related training, and subsequently provide on-site support and training to the facilitators implementing Suraksha activities in the schools. The position requires a proactive, responsible and field-oriented individual who can build positive relationships with schools, work closely with facilitators and local stakeholders, observe programme implementation closely, and ensure that activities are completed effectively and documented appropriately. Key Responsibilities 1. Facilitator Training and Support * Receive continuous guidance, mentoring and appropriate training from the Suraksha Programme Manager. * Conduct on-site training, orientation and handholding support for facilitators in the three project schools. * Regularly interact with facilitators to understand implementation challenges and provide support within the scope of the programme. * Identify training and capacity-building needs and communicate these to the Suraksha Programme Manager. * Ensure that facilitators understand the objectives, methodology and safeguarding principles of the Suraksha programme. 2. School Coordination and Relationship Building * Maintain regular and professional communication with the three project schools—Ranarani, Banpukhuria and Manikpara. * With the support of the local Field Coordinator, develop and maintain a positive working relationship with the concerned government school authorities, teachers and other relevant stakeholders. * Coordinate with schools to facilitate smooth implementation of programme activities. * Communicate the programme schedule and requirements to the concerned school personnel in a timely manner. 3. Programme Planning and Implementation * Prepare and maintain a programme calendar in consultation with the Suraksha Programme Manager and the respective schools. * Plan frequent field visits and travel between the three project schools, keeping the Suraksha Programme Manager informed and obtaining necessary guidance. * Be personally present during Suraksha-related activities wherever required to ensure smooth and effective implementation. * Observe programme sessions and activities closely and provide constructive feedback to facilitators. * Ensure that planned activities are implemented according to the programme framework, timelines and quality standards. * Identify field-level challenges and escalate them promptly to the Suraksha Programme Manager. 4. Monitoring, Observation and Documentation * Regularly monitor programme implementation across all three schools. * Document key observations, participation, progress, challenges, outcomes and significant developments. * Maintain appropriate records, reports, photographs and other programme documentation as required. * Support the Suraksha Programme Manager in compiling periodic programme updates, progress reports and outcome documentation. * Ensure that programme records are accurate, timely and properly maintained. 5. Coordination with Mukti Team * Work collaboratively with the Suraksha Programme Manager, MSS Coordinators, HR team and other relevant Mukti personnel. * Participate in online meetings, review meetings and programme discussions as required. * Maintain timely communication with the concerned team members regarding field activities, progress, challenges and emerging concerns. * Follow Mukti's organisational policies, procedures and professional standards at all times. 6. Child Safeguarding and Gender * Demonstrate a clear understanding of child safeguarding, child rights, gender equality, adolescent well-being and prevention of abuse and exploitation. * Ensure that all programme activities are conducted in a safe, respectful, inclusive and child-sensitive manner. * Familiarity with child protection mechanisms, safeguarding principles, gender-related programmes or adolescent-focused interventions will be considered a strong advantage. * Strictly adhere to Mukti's Child Safeguarding Policy and POSH Policy and immediately report any safeguarding concern through the appropriate organisational channels. Required Qualifications and Competencies Essential * The candidate must be a resident of Jhargram district. * Minimum Graduate degree from a recognised institution. * A certificate, diploma or degree or work experience in Child Protection, Child Rights, Social Work, Gender Studies, Development Studies or a related discipline will be highly preferred. * Basic computer literacy with the ability to: o prepare and maintain documents and reports; o use email effectively; o participate in online meetings; o maintain basic digital records and documentation. * Ability to understand and communicate in simple English, both verbally and in writing. * Good communication and interpersonal skills. * Willingness and ability to undertake frequent field travel between the three project schools in Jhargram. * Ability to work independently in the field while remaining closely connected with the Programme Manager and the wider Mukti team. Desirable * Prior experience working with children, adolescents, schools, child protection, gender, safeguarding or community-based programmes. * Formal training or certification in child safeguarding, child rights, gender or related areas. * Experience of working with government schools or community-based organisations. * Ability to facilitate group sessions, training or orientation programmes. * Sensitivity, maturity and confidence in handling child- and gender-related issues. Key Personal Attributes The ideal candidate should be: * Child-sensitive, empathetic and responsible * Proactive and willing to work extensively in the field * A good listener and communicator * Organised and attentive to documentation * Comfortable working with school authorities, teachers and community stakeholders * Open to learning and receiving continuous supervision and feedback * Able to maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries * Committed to safeguarding, gender equality and creating safe spaces for children and adolescents Nature of the Role This is a field-intensive coordination role requiring regular movement between the three project schools. The Coordinator is expected not merely to coordinate activities remotely, but to remain physically present, observe implementation, support facilitators, build school relationships, identify challenges and document programme outcomes. The role offers an opportunity to contribute directly to creating safer, more inclusive and gender-sensitive school environments for children and adolescents in Jhargram. Remuneration: 12,000 per month + TA on actual basis.

description: Request for Proposal National Study on Truck Drivers in India_August'2026 Title of the Study: Comprehensive National Study on the Health, Well-being and Occupational Conditions of Truck Drivers in India Background India’s road transport sector carries nearly 70% of the country’s freight movement and commercial truck drivers form the backbone of the national economy. Despite their critical contribution, truck drivers remain one of the most underserved occupational groups. Long working hours, irregular schedules, poor living conditions during transit, occupational hazards, limited healthcare access, inadequate social protection, financial insecurity and changing industry dynamics adversely affect their health, productivity and quality of life. Apollo Tyres Foundation (ATF) is the Corporate Social Responsibility arm of Apollo Tyres Ltd. ATF works towards enhancing stakeholder value through sustainable and scalable social development initiatives aligned with the Company's business objectives and ESG commitments. ATF has been implementing healthcare interventions for the trucking community since 2000 through a network of healthcare centres across India, delivering preventive, promotive and curative healthcare services. Purpose of the Study The purpose of this study is to generate nationally representative evidence on the multidimensional challenges faced by truck drivers in India and develop actionable recommendations for improving their health, safety, welfare, productivity and quality of life. The study should go beyond disease prevalence and examine the broader determinants influencing health, including occupational, economic, social, behavioural, environmental and policy-related factors. Overall Objective: To comprehensively assess the health status, occupational conditions, socio-economic circumstances, healthcare access, and overall quality of life of truck drivers in India, and identify the key factors influencing their health, well-being, productivity and livelihood for informing evidence-based policies and interventions. Specific Objectives: 1. Economical & Social Protection Assess employment stability and welfare coverage: Evaluate working conditions, job security, income dynamics and driver awareness/utilization of government social security and health schemes (e.g., e-Shram, PM-JAY, Ayushman Bharat). 2. Health & Wellbeing Evaluate physical and mental health status: Assess overall physical, psychological, and social health outcomes (including burnout and stress) as well as drivers' healthcare-seeking behaviours and access to medical care. 3. Occupational Hazards & Living Conditions Examine working environment and transit infrastructure: Investigate driving hours, rest patterns, ergonomics, fatigue, environmental hazards, and substance use, alongside the availability and quality of highway facilities (parking, sanitation, water, and rest zones). 4. Regional Variations, Aspirations & Policy Roadmap Map corridor variations and formulate stakeholder recommendations: Identify regional/corridor-wise differences, document drivers' future career perceptions and formulate evidence-based policy roadmaps for government bodies, fleet owners, healthcare providers and industry associations. Scope of Work: The proposed study will undertake a comprehensive, pan-India assessment of the health, occupational, socio-economic and living conditions of truck drivers using a mixed-method research approach. The assignment will include an extensive review of existing literature, stakeholder consultations, development of a robust research framework, study protocol, sampling strategy and survey instruments, followed by pilot testing and refinement of tools. The agency will conduct nationally representative quantitative surveys, qualitative research (including focus group discussions, in-depth interviews, and key informant interviews) and field observations across major transport corridors, logistics hubs and truck halt points to assess physical, mental and occupational health, employment conditions, healthcare access, utilisation of government welfare schemes, transit infrastructure, road safety, working conditions and quality of life. The study will also examine the social, economic, behavioural, environmental and systemic determinants influencing truck drivers' health and productivity, analyse regional variations and benchmark findings against national and international best practices. In addition, the agency will undertake GIS mapping of critical support infrastructure, estimate the economic burden of poor health and occupational risks, develop a Truck Driver Health & Well-being Index and identify gaps in existing policies, programmes and CSR interventions. The assignment will culminate in the preparation of a comprehensive national report, policy briefs, state and corridor-specific fact sheets, advocacy materials, dissemination workshops and evidence-based recommendations for governments, industry, healthcare providers and CSR organisations to strengthen policies and interventions aimed at improving the health, safety, welfare and overall quality of life of truck drivers in India. 1. description: ABOUT SNEHA SNEHA (Society for Nutrition, Education and Health Action) is a Mumbai-based non-profit organization dedicated to improving the health, nutrition, and safety of women and children living in vulnerable urban informal settlements. Our mission is to empower urban women and children through integrated health and nutrition programs, education, and advocacy. We work through a dual approach—engaging both care seekers and care providers. At the community level, we empower women and families to become agents of change, while simultaneously collaborating with public health and safety systems to drive sustainable improvements in urban health outcomes. SNEHA’s key programs include: Maternal and Child Health Empowerment, Health and Sexuality of Adolescents Prevention of Violence against Women and Children Public System Partnership Palliative Care Between 2016 and 2025, SNEHA directly reached over 620,555 women, children, and healthcare workers, and indirectly impacted a population of over 3.63 million across seven municipal corporations and three municipal councils in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR). Today, SNEHA is a 500+ member organization with deep grassroots presence and a strong track record of reducing maternal and neonatal mortality, child malnutrition, adolescent anemia, and gender-based violence— key determinants of health equity for families and communities. ABOUT THE PROJECT Maternal and Child Health – Strategy and Implementation (MCH-SI) – Building Bridges is a direct intervention program working in 10,000 households in Bhiwandi since 2016, in collaboration with the public health and nutrition systems. It spans 12 intervention areas, covering 5 health posts and the Indira Gandhi Memorial Hospital. The program aims to improve the health and nutrition of women and children in underserved urban communities, focusing on Married Women of Reproductive Age (19–49 years): antenatal/postnatal care and family planning counseling. Children (0–6 years): immunization, nutrition, home-based care for low-birth-weight babies, breastfeeding support, and management of infectious diseases. The MCH team, frontline workers, and volunteers conduct home visits, counseling, and community awareness drives (street plays, exhibitions, campaigns) on breastfeeding, complementary feeding, immunization, and hygiene. They also strengthen the public health system through immunization camps, volunteer training, and capacity building of ICDS Sevikas and ASHAs. “WHAT’S IN IT FOR ME” (WIIFM) - AT SNEHA At SNEHA, our fundamental belief is that prioritizing people is key, demonstrating our strong dedication to nurturing a supportive and growth-driven atmosphere. We uphold an open-door policy that champions transparency and open dialogue. We actively invite employees to voice their ideas, feedback, and concerns, fostering a culture where innovation and teamwork can flourish. If you value excellence and are passionate about nurturing individuals, SNEHA is the perfect place for you!! For detailed Information visit our website: www.snehamumbai.org PROFILE SNAPSHOT Designation: Community Organizer Role: Planning and implementing project activities in coordination with Program Officer (PO) and field team. Building and sustaining effective rapport with different stakeholders including health facilities staff and community members. Educational Requirement: 12th Passed Experience: Minimum 1-2 years of relevant experience in community development with any of the two of the thematic area (maternal & child health, family planning and working with social welfare dept of govt.). Freshers with strong volunteer experience in the same field may also apply Location: BHIWANDI NIZAMPUR CITY MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (BNCMC). Willingness to travel within Mumbai and willing to participate for exposure visits in other states of India. Reports to: Program Officer Apply: Applications are to be sent via email to belinda.menezes@snehamumbai.org with the Subject line: “Community Organizer- BBD” COMPREHENSIVE OVERVIEW OF THE POSITION This role is responsible for planning, coordinating, and monitoring field activities to strengthen maternal and child health interventions. The position involves leading community mobilization efforts, building the capacities of health staff and volunteers, supporting referral linkages, and ensuring effective engagement with stakeholders. CORE DUTIES 1. Community Outreach & Home Visits Conduct regular home visits to children, pregnant and lactating women, and families. Support protocol-based RMNCH (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Child Health) visits. Conduct menstrual surveillance and identify pregnant women for early registration. Form and strengthen community groups and facilitate regular community meetings. 2. Maternal, Child Health & Nutrition Monitor child health, growth, and nutrition, including anthropometric assessments of low birth weight (LBW) children. Provide counselling on maternal health, child health, nutrition, immunization, breastfeeding, and family planning. Identify high-risk mothers and children, facilitate timely referrals, and ensure follow-up of health services. Mobilize families for immunization, growth monitoring, antenatal and postnatal care, and other essential health services. 3. Community Mobilization & Volunteer Engagement Identify, mobilize, and mentor community volunteers and ASHAs. Conduct regular volunteer meetings, trainings, and supportive supervision. Build volunteers' capacities on health, nutrition, community mobilization, and facilitation skills. Strengthen linkages between volunteers and government health systems to improve service delivery. Support volunteers during home visits and community events to enhance outreach and community participation. 4. Coordination & Stakeholder Engagement Coordinate with ICDS, ASHAs, Anganwadi Workers, health facilities, and other community stakeholders. Support joint field visits, special health days, and community-based events. Facilitate community participation through group meetings and promote access to health and social protection services. 5. Documentation & Reporting Maintain beneficiary records and update program data regularly using CommCare and other reporting formats. Prepare monthly case stories and maintain volunteer-related documentation. Ensure timely and accurate reporting of field activities, referrals, and program outcomes. CRITICAL TRAITS Fluency in Marathi and Hindi (Basic English preferred) Ability to work in community and field settings Basic documentation and record-keeping skills Willingness to travel within assigned villages/communities Interest in community health and social development Ability to coordinate with ASHAs, Anganwadi Workers, and community volunteers BEHAVIORAL COMPETENCIES Good communication and interpersonal skills Ability to build rapport with community members and frontline workers Teamwork and collaboration Willingness to learn and take initiative Responsible, reliable, and adaptable Basic problem-solving skills “Come and be a catalyst for innovation and positive change—apply today to shape the future with us!”

description: State Lead - Maharashtra Organisation's Profile Transform Schools is working to ensure that every child realises their full potential in school and beyond. We co-design and implement evidence-based education programmes with State governments, with a focus on strengthening foundational learning, building equitable learning environments, and preparing students for transitions beyond school. Our work combines pedagogical innovation, teacher development, data-driven instruction, and systemic reform to ensure every adolescent—especially those from underserved communities—can thrive. As co-convenors of the State of Secondary Education (SOSE) global collaborative, we are also shaping a global agenda to position secondary education as a societal minimum standard—mobilising research, investment, and practice across the Global South. Our work spans two institutional vehicles: People For Action, a charitable society that delivers CSR and grant-funded programmes, and The Transform Trust, which leads outcomes-linked engagements. With a strong footprint across multiple States (Definite plans for expansion and deepening of our work) and a commitment to scale, we aim to reach 30 million children by 2030, building a future where quality secondary education is a reality for all. Job Purpose The State Lead will be responsible for leading the implementation, scaling, and institutionalisation of the programmes in partnership with the Maharashtra Education Commission (MEC), State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Samagra Shiksha, and other relevant stakeholders. The position will focus on building state-level ownership of the programme, ensuring alignment with Maharashtra's education priorities, building strategic partnerships with government bodies, and driving sustainable impact across the state's public education system. This role requires strong leadership, advocacy, partnership-building, and systems-thinking to implement long-lasting, scalable education models. Key Responsibilities 1. Engage directly with the Principal Secretary, State Project Director, SCERT, and the MEC to ensure the programme aligns with the state's educational reform goals and priorities. Act as the key liaison between Transform Schools and state-level stakeholders to ensure the successful integration of the programme into state policies and strategies. Develop and maintain strong relationships with government stakeholders (e.g., MEC, SCERT, Samagra Shiksha) to build collaboration and ensure the sustainability of the programme. Build partnerships with civil society organisations, NGOs, and industry players (e.g., Nirmaan, Learning Curve, CSF, CEGIS, LFE) to leverage their expertise, resources, and networks. Identify opportunities for programme adaptation based on the State's political mandate, educational needs, and long-term vision. 2. Advocacy and Policy Influence Advocate for the integration of the TS programmes within the State's existing educational frameworks and policies. Ensure that the programmes are prioritised within the State's annual budget allocation, thereby facilitating funding for the models. Co-create scale interventions with government counterparts, ensuring that these interventions respond to systemic challenges in the public education sector. Collaborate with state stakeholders to design and implement interventions that drive systemic impact, with a focus on sustainability and state ownership. 3. Programme Implementation, technology integration, financial management and quality Lead implementation and tracking of Transform Programmes in the State, along with integration of technology systems, integration into high priority governance processes. Lead internal team and build capacity for high-quality, outcome-focused implementation, government liaison, data-based management and systems change principles. Ensure effective implementation of programmes in selected schools to ensure an agreed outcome to showcase to the CMs office. Plan and ensure timely support to the State(s) government in distribution of all teaching and learning resources for training and school-level implementation. Lead planning and delivery of capacity building for government officials, Master Trainers, Head Teachers, teachers and other stakeholders to deliver Transform Programmes. Review, analyse and lead reflection on programme progress through data Management Information Systems to plan action and advocacy initiatives. Plan, track and report on budget utilisation as per monthly and quarterly milestones; review planned activities and actual expenditure. Ensure that partners (such as technical agencies and State education departments) submit programme and financial documents as per agreement. Contribute during ideation for new projects or deepening existing programmes. 4. Share a monthly report to the Lead - Programme Design and Quality, on the progress, including data on syllabus completion, pre-post assessments, student participation, observation reports on teaching practices and status of teaching–learning facilities. Build collaboration among ecosystem partners, ensuring that best practices are shared, and stakeholders are aligned towards a common goal. description: Position: District Coordinator, Presbyopia Program (District-based, Chhattisgarh) Overview: WJCF is an Indian non-profit organisation committed to saving lives by reducing the burden of disease and strengthening government-owned, high-quality health systems. Since 2007, WJCF has combined data-driven approaches and deep public health expertise with strong government partnerships to design, implement, and scale solutions across India’s national and state health programmes. We work for and at the service of governments — supporting the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and State Departments of Health to build systems that are strong, sustainable, and led by Indian institutions. As an Indian organisation, WJCF brings an unmatched depth of contextual understanding of India’s health system architecture, policy landscape, and implementation realities across diverse geographies and population groups. This local institutional credibility, combined with global technical rigour, is central to WJCF’s effectiveness as a partner to governments and donors. Our work is built around four complementary roles: as a Trusted Government Partner, co-designing programmes and strengthening health system architecture; as an Operational Partner, translating strategies into effective on-the-ground delivery; as a Market Shaper, improving the availability and affordability of health commodities; and as an Ecosystem Catalyst, convening governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector to drive solutions at scale. WJCF’s programme portfolio spans thematic areas like hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases, syphilis, cervical cancer, diabetes, maternal and childhood anaemia, immunisation, under-5 diarrhoea and pneumonia, sexual and reproductive health, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri – Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), hypoxemia and oxygen, safe drinking water, sickle cell disease, presbyopia, lead poisoning, and cross cutting thematic areas like AI and Health, integrated disease surveillance and climate and health. We currently support programmes across 19 states and union territories, with teams working at national, state, district, and sub-district levels. Our people are our greatest asset. WJCF brings together a talented, diverse team of professionals from public health, analytics, consulting, healthcare, the development sector, and academia, all united by a shared commitment to improving health outcomes for the people of India. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and deeply grounded in the communities and systems we work in. Our field teams collectively bring hundreds of years of experience managing public health programmes across the country. WJCF collaborates with a range of international and domestic partners and donors to advance its mission, including an affiliation with the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), a global health organisation with which WJCF shares a common mission and values. Programme Overview: Presbyopia is an age-related condition characterized by the gradual loss of the ability to see objects clearly up close that affects over one billion people globally. It is estimated that approximately 150 million live with uncorrected presbyopia in India. When unaddressed, presbyopia severely impacts daily life and job performance, particularly in occupations requiring clear near vision. Unaddressed presbyopia is estimated to adversely impact India's GDP by $14 billion annually. Presbyopia can be corrected with near vision glasses (also known as reading glasses) which has shown to increase income by 28% and productivity by 30%. The National Program for Control of Blindness and Vision Impairment (NPCBVI), launched by the Government of India in 1976, has evolved to address not only blindness from cataracts but also the burden of refractive errors. NPCBVI mandates for effective screening and management of presbyopia as part of its refractive-error interventions with the larger aim to enhance the quality of life for older adults and contribute to national goals of equitable eye-care access. In line with these priorities, the William J. Clinton Foundation (WJCF) is planning to implement a project across 8 districts of Chhattisgarh to improve access to presbyopia care through a decentralized model. Project Background: The William J. Clinton Foundation (WJCF) aims to strengthen the public health system’s readiness and capacity to expand access to presbyopia care by integrating eye screening and on-site dispensation of near vision glasses within primary healthcare settings. To advance this objective, WJCF is planning to implement decentralized presbyopia care across 8 districts of Chhattisgarh. The project will focus on generating operational learnings, implementation insights, and evidence-based approaches that can inform scalable models for state-wide adoption. As part of the initiative, WJCF will support the capacity building of healthcare workers—including primary-level staff and frontline health workers—on presbyopia identification, screening protocols, counselling, and referral pathways, thereby strengthening the delivery of comprehensive eye-care services at the primary-care level. These efforts will be complemented by community engagement and awareness activities designed to improve understanding of presbyopia, encourage timely care-seeking, and enhance the uptake of near-vision correction and comprehensive eye care. Position Summary: WJCF is looking to hire 8 District Coordinators to lead on-ground implementation of the presbyopia program in an assigned district of Chhattisgarh. The position is field-based and requires ability to drive project delivery in close coordination with district and block government officials. The District Coordinator is responsible for all programme components within the assigned district and will also provide implementation support in assigned blocks. We are seeking a highly motivated, entrepreneurial individual with outstanding program implementation capabilities. The candidate must be able to function independently and have a strong commitment to excellence. WJCF places great value on relevant personal qualities: resourcefulness, humility, responsibility, accountability, tenacity, independence, energy, and attention to detail. Responsibilities: Lead implementation of operational plans in the assigned district; provide dedicated implementation support in 2-3 blocks; and manage relationships with district-level government and non-government stakeholders, including CMHO, District Programme Managers, and other district authorities. Support the rollout of data reporting, monitoring, and evaluation tools to track program performance. Facilitate collection and analysis of facility- and community-level data to identify field-level gaps and improvement areas. Conduct training sessions for healthcare workers using standardized training materials and eye-screening protocols. Coordinate with NCD clinics and Vision Centers in the assigned district to operationalise referral mechanisms for presbyopia screening; support integration into routine OPD and NCD clinic workflows; and monitor near vision glass dispensation and stock availability at Vision Centers. Support implementation of forecasting and inventory management plans, including rollout of stock monitoring tools and dashboards to ensure uninterrupted commodity supply. Prepare documentation and communication materials such as reports, briefs, and updates for government, donor, and other stakeholders. Travel at short notice to project districts or to the state office in Raipur, as required. Perform any other responsibilities assigned by the program leadership. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in economics/public health/business or a related field and a minimum of five years of professional experience in program implementation. Proven ability to communicate effectively and engage with government officials and community stakeholders. Experience in data collection, analysis, and utilization for program evaluation and decision-making. Working knowledge in MS Office. Entrepreneurial mindset with demonstrated ability to work independently on complex projects and solve challenging problems, in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment Demonstrated ability to multi-task with a strong commitment to excellence. Hindi language fluency (both written and verbal); working knowledge of Chhattisgarhi preferred. Apply Here: Link to District Coordinator - Here

title: Manager - Program Strategy & Operations
description: Salary Rs 75,000 – 85,000/month CTC Experience 4–5 years Start Date As soon as possible Working Hours 8 hrs/day, flexible 9:30 am – 6:30 pm Reporting Manager Director —Strategy and Programs Languages English and Hindi required; Marathi or regional language preferred ABOUT SOL'S ARC Sol's ARC is an NGO that works to ensure every child learns and every adult earns. For over 20 years, we have worked with governments, donors and communities to create lasting change for Persons with Disabilities — through inclusive education, vocational skilling and livelihood programmes across multiple states. THE ROLE This is a mid-to-senior role for someone who is good at turning plans into action. You will manage the day-to-day delivery of Sol's ARC's programmes, keep teams on track, handle donor reporting, and ensure the Director of program and Strategy has everything she needs to lead externally. This is a hands-on role — you will be expected to solve problems, coordinate teams across locations, and be accountable for outcomes.It requires to travel to field locations . HOW YOU'LL SPEND YOUR TIME 50% Programme planning and operations 20% Monitoring, reporting and donor compliance 15% Team coordination and capacity building 15% Stakeholder liaison and internal alignment WHAT YOU'LL DO Track work plans and operations per program Track all Sol's ARC programmes — inclusive education, skilling, livelihoods — are running on time and within budget. Build work plans, activity calendars and milestone trackers for each programme. Review progress every week with state and field teams. Travel every quarter for one week to engagement and understand ground realities Track programme budgets with the Finance team. Make sure expenses match the donor agreement heads. Prepare utilisation certificates on time. Manage programme changes, scale-ups and closures as needed. Reporting and donor compliance Build a reporting system that gives accurate and timely data to donors, government partners and the leadership team. Write programme progress reports and review financial reports. Make sure all reports match agreed milestones and indicators. Work with the M&E team to track what has been done and what outcomes have been achieved. Keep all programme documents — SOPs, field protocols, frameworks — organised and up to date. Flag risks and problems to the Director early, with your suggested solutions. Team coordination and capacity building Coordinate with programme, M&E, finance, HR and communications teams to keep delivery on track. Directly support state-level coordinators and team leads — help them plan, execute and report. Run regular team meetings and review sessions. Help new programme staff settle into their roles. Stakeholder liaison and internal alignment Be the main point of contact for government departments and implementation partners on day-to-day programme matters. Prepare briefing notes, updates and presentation materials for the Director to use in meetings with government, donors and the Board. Represent Sol's ARC in partner coordination meetings when required. WHAT'S HARD ABOUT THIS ROLE Managing several programmes at once — each with different donors, deadlines and field realities. Working in a fast-changing environment where priorities shift quickly. Building trust and accountability with field teams you may rarely meet in person. Keeping delivery on track while government systems move slowly. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR Qualifications and experience Master's degree in Social Work, Development Studies, Public Policy, MBA or a related field. Strong practical experience will be considered in place of qualifications. 4–5 years of experience in programme operations or project management, with at least 2 years managing multi-location, multi-donor programmes in a nonprofit or development sector organisation. Experience managing field teams across multiple states or districts. Strong track record of donor reporting, MoU compliance and milestone-based accountability. Experience working with government bodies (education, social justice, skill development) is an advantage. Familiarity with the RPwD Act, NEP 2020 or NIPUN Bharat is preferred. Skills Strong planning and organisational skills — can manage multiple workstreams without losing track of detail. Clear written communication — can write donor reports and programme briefs independently. Comfortable working with MIS systems, dashboards and outcome data. Works well with others but can drive accountability and make decisions when needed. Takes ownership — does not wait to be told; anticipates problems and resolves them. What makes an exceptional candidate All programmes delivered on time, within budget, and with no surprises at the end of a reporting period. The Director spends her time on strategy and external engagement — not chasing programme updates. Field teams feel supported, clear on their targets, and accountable. Donors receive accurate, insightful reports that reflect real programme progress. WHAT WE OFFER • Salary as per Sol's ARC pay scale, based on your experience. • Travel reimbursement for all programme-related travel. • Outcomes-based flexible work — targets are clear; how you plan your day is up to you. • Training and support from the programme team when you join.

description: CONSTRUCTION AGENCY- Upgradation of Government Composite School inHazipur Khera and In-Drain Treatment System in Vilasganj, Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India INTRODUCTION Hazipur Khera, Agra has been finalised for a school upgradation and Vilasganj for In-drain treatment system projects by CURE to improve the school infrastructure and learning environment to sustain children in school and treating the drain water before draining it into the Kalwari pond. The aim of the project is to enhance school enrolment and participation by improving school infrastructure, especially water and sanitation and to improve the water quality of the Kalwari pond. ABOUT THE ORGANISATION Founded in 2001, the Centre for Urban and Regional Excellence (CURE) is a non-profit organization committed to nurturing inclusive and sustainable development within India's urban, informal, and low-income communities. Employing a hyperlocal, ecosystem-centered approach, CURE places a strong emphasis on community engagement, valuing residents as crucial partners and leaders. Its initiatives span from facilitating access to vital services such as household toilets and clean water taps to empowering livelihoods through skill development and small-scale enterprises. SCOPE OF WORK The infrastructural upgradation of Government Composite School in Kalwari, Agra will involve: A. HAZIPUR KHERA Construction of New child friendly student toilet block- 61.24 m2 area. Demolition of old students’ toilet and Construction of new Staff toilet on it- 19.125 m2 area. Construction of DEWATS- connected through new student’s toilet block- 12.74 Meters, Approx 22000 Liters capacity. Retrofitting of existing Classrooms, Staff office, Kitchen and Storeroom. description: About Anahat Anahat For Change Foundation is a women-led organisation established in 2018, working towards a gender-just society where women and adolescents can exercise their rights with dignity. Anahat works at the intersection of gender, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), menstrual health, and sustainable livelihoods. Through community-led approaches, it works with underserved rural and tribal communities while strengthening linkages with government systems and local institutions. About Project Unnati Project Unnati is Anahat For Change Foundation’s community-led menstrual health and livelihood programme in Jharkhand. The programme works with women and adolescent girls to improve menstrual health knowledge, increase access to affordable and sustainable menstrual products, and address myths and stigma around menstruation. It builds a network of trained Unnati Didis who mobilise communities, conduct awareness activities and facilitate access to sustainable menstrual products. The programme also promotes local production & selling of reusable cloth pads by women, creating livelihood opportunities while strengthening the last-mile supply chain. Project Unnati works closely with JSLPS, Panchayats, schools, health workers and government departments to strengthen community ownership and long-term sustainability. Role Purpose The Livelihood Programme Manager will lead the field implementation of Project Unnati in Jharkhand, with responsibility for achieving menstrual health outreach, sustainable product adoption, livelihood, school engagement and government convergence targets. The Programme Manager will directly lead a grassroots team comprising approximately 40 active women and three Cluster Coordinators, and will be responsible for translating the programme strategy into monthly and quarterly field-level action plans. The role requires someone with strong experience in leading grassroots teams, community mobilisation, government liaison and target-based programme implementation. Key Roles & Responsibilities I. Programme Planning & Team Leadership 1.Develop annual, quarterly and monthly work plans in alignment with Project Unnati targets and timelines. 2.Lead and supervise a grassroots team of approximately 40 active women and three Cluster Coordinators across Dumka and Koderma 3.Conduct regular review meetings with Cluster Coordinators and field teams to assess progress, identify challenges and develop corrective action plans. 4.Ensure clear allocation of villages, schools, activities and targets across Cluster Coordinators and field teams. II. Livelihood, Product Access & Sales 1.Ensure that Cluster Coordinators and Unnati Didis achieve agreed menstrual product selling/adoption targets within their respective clusters. 2.Regularly monitor sales, stock movement, demand generation, product uptake and performance against targets. 3.Manage the reusable menstrual product supply chain, including coordination between cloth-pad makers, Unnati Didis, Cluster Coordinators and the project team. 4.Oversee the revolving fund mechanism, including product distribution, recovery, incentives and reinvestment into subsequent product cycles. 5.Coordinate with JSLPS, SHGs and local women’s groups for strengthening local production and livelihood opportunities. Project Unnati's existing model combines community-level menstrual health awareness with local distribution and livelihood opportunities for women. III. Community & Health Activities 1.Ensure that planned menstrual health and other health camps are organised in project villages according to the approved work plan. 2.Coordinate community mobilisation for health camps and ensure participation of women, adolescent girls, frontline health workers and other relevant stakeholders. 3.Facilitate linkages with appropriate government health facilities and frontline workers for referrals and follow-up wherever required. 4.Ensure community-level menstrual health awareness activities are conducted regularly and effectively. IV. School Engagement 1.Ensure that all planned school-based menstrual health sessions are conducted on time and according to the programme calendar. 2.Liaise with schools, teachers and relevant education authorities to obtain necessary coordination and support. 3.Monitor school session quality, attendance, documentation and follow-up. 4.Coordinate school-level health activities wherever planned under the programme. V. Government Convergence & Liaison 1.Build and maintain working relationships with Panchayats, JSLPS, local administrative offices, Health Department, School/Education Department and other relevant Government of Jharkhand departments. 2.Ensure regular government dissemination and stakeholder meetings to share programme progress, challenges, evidence and learning. 3.Prepare and submit monthly programme progress reports to relevant government departments, wherever agreed with the respective authorities. 4.Represent Project Unnati in block-, Panchayat- and district-level meetings as required. 5.Work towards strengthening convergence between Unnati Didis, ASHA/Sahiya workers, schools, Panchayats, SHGs and government systems. The existing Unnati model already envisages Unnati Didis working alongside ASHA workers and regular engagement with village administration and relevant stakeholders. VI. Resource Mobilisation & Panchayat Convergence 1.Identify opportunities to mobilise Panchayat-level funds and available government resources for menstrual health activities, community awareness programmes, health camps and related interventions. 2.Engage Panchayat representatives to integrate menstrual health activities into locally supported community initiatives. 3.Explore convergence with existing government schemes and programmes so that activities can progressively be supported through public systems rather than remaining completely grant-dependent. VII. Monitoring, Reporting & Documentation 1.Track cluster-wise targets related to community outreach, product adoption/sales, school sessions, health camps, government engagement and livelihood activities. 2.Maintain updated programme MIS and review data regularly with Cluster Coordinators. Prepare monthly progress reports highlighting achievements against targets, challenges, corrective actions and priorities for the following month. 3.Ensure timely documentation of field activities, beneficiary records, product movement, meetings, health camps and government engagement. 4.Collect field-level feedback and ensure that learning is incorporated into subsequent programme planning. VIII. Capacity Building & Training 1.Ensure timely training and capacity sharing of government and community stakeholders on menstrual health, including JSLPS cadres, government frontline workers, school teachers and active women/community leaders. 2.Coordinate training calendars, participant mobilisation, trainers, venues and required training materials. 3.Ensure that trained stakeholders receive appropriate IEC/BCC materials, facilitator resources and menstrual health information materials for use within schools and communities. 4.Monitor whether IEC materials are being effectively disseminated and used by Unnati Didis, JSLPS cadres, frontline workers, teachers and other trained stakeholders. 5.Conduct/refacilitate refresher trainings wherever knowledge gaps or implementation challenges are identified. 6.Maintain training records, attendance, pre/post assessments and documentation for programme and government reporting. Candidate Profile Job Location & Working Hours 1.Location: Koderma, Jharkhand. The Programme Manager will be expected to work primarily from Anahat’s Koderma office, with regular field travel across project villages. 2.Working Days: Monday to Saturday, with the 1st and 3rd Saturdays of every month as holidays. The Programme Manager will also be expected to travel to Anahat’s Kolkata office for reporting, review meetings, training and capacity-building purposes, as and when required. Required Qualifications & Experience 1.Experience: Minimum 5–8 years of professional experience in the Social Development Sector, with a proven track record in Livelihood programs and grassroots community work. Having experience in the sustainable menstrual product sector will add value. 2.SHG & JSLPS Expertise:4 to 10 years of hands-on experience working alongside State Rural Livelihood Missions (JSLPS) and Self-Help Group (SHG) federations. 3.Value Chain / Market Linkage: Proven ability in creating demand-and-supply networks and enterprise models at the community level. 4.Team Leadership: Prior experience managing and supporting field teams. 5.Education: Graduate/Post-Graduate degree in Sales & Marketing, Social Work (MSW), Rural Development, Management, or related social science disciplines. Preferred / Added Value Prior experience in the Menstrual Health & Hygiene (MHM) space, specifically in promoting, distributing, or marketing reusable cloth pads or sustainable health solutions. Language Proficiency: Fluency in Hindi is required; knowledge of local Jharkhand dialects/languages is a strong plus. description: Job Description: Course Design Expert Department: Talent Management C Learning and Development Reports to: Programme Lead, Talent Management C LCD Location: Dr. Shroff's Charity Eye Hospital (SCEH), Delhi Nature of Role: Full-time, with cross-departmental reach Position Summary: SCEH is building a portfolio of courses and training programs that eventually will become the benchmark for eyecare education, not just within the organisation but across the sector, in India C globally. The Course Design Expert is the person who will turn this goal into reality. This role is under the Talent Management C LCD but works across the SCEH group, partnering with Medical Education (MED), Allied Ophthalmic Personnel (AOP), Public Health and clinical and administrative departments to design and develop training programs from the ground up. The person takes a department's inherent expertise, of senior clinicians or program leads and converts it into a structured course with clear objectives, defined competencies, sound pedagogy and content that benchmarks against global standards. The role has two distinct part that require different strengths. The first is architectural: working with a department to define what a course should achieve and how it should be structured. The second is developmental: working with faculty (internal and external) to actually build the content, sequence it well and make sure it imparts knowledge, skills, competencies C bring about behaviour change. Key Responsibilities: 1. Course Architecture s Design: • Partner with requesting departments (MED, AOP, Public Health and others) to translate a training need into a formal course structure with course objectives, learning objectives, expected outcomes and the specific competencies to be developed. • Determine the right pedagogical approach for each course (classroom, simulation, on-the-job, blended, self-paced) based on the competency being built and not by defaulting to one format. • Define learning hours and course duration in a way which is realistic for working clinical and support staff and commensurate with the depth of competency required. • Build assessment frameworks that genuinely measure whether the stated learning objectives were met, rather than traditional tools of assessment. 2. Content Development s Faculty Collaboration: • Once a course structure is approved, work directly with identified faculty, both internal SCEH experts and external subject matter experts, to develop the actual training content. • Ensure content draws on SCEH's own rich clinical and operational knowledge first and is supplemented with best practice and evidence from national and global sources where it strengthens the course. • Review and edit faculty-submitted content for instructional soundness with regards to sequencing, clarity, cognitive load and alignment back to the course's stated objectives. • Manage the handoff between subject expertise and instructional design, since faculty are usually strong on content but not on how adults learn. 3. Quality, Standards s Benchmarking: • Establish and maintain a consistent quality bar across all SCEH courses integrating its ethos C values, so that a course built for various depts feel like they come from the same institution. • Keep a working knowledge of instructional design standards and eyecare training practices globally and use that knowledge to push SCEH courses toward a world-class benchmark rather than a locally adequate one. • Build reusable templates and design frameworks (course design canvas, competency mapping tools, faculty briefing formats) so course quality doesn't depend on reinventing the process each time. 4. Stakeholder s Program Management: • Act as the primary LCD point of contact for departments that want a new course built or an existing one redesigned. • Manage multiple course design projects concurrently, across departments with different timelines, priorities and levels of instructional design maturity. • Report progress, risks and course performance to the Programme Lead and relevant department heads. • Where relevant, contribute to piloting new courses, gathering feedback from the first cohort and revising the course before it is scaled. KRA: Description: Indicative Measures: Course Structures Delivered: Number and quality of complete course frameworks (objectives, outcomes, competencies, pedagogy, learning hours) delivered to requesting departments Courses designed per quarter; department sign-off on structure before content development begins Content Quality s Turnaround: Faculty-developed content reviewed, refined and finalized within agreed timelines Average time from structure approval to content-ready stage; revision cycles needed per course Cross-Departmental Partnership: Depth and quality of working relationships with MED, AOP, Public Health and other departments requesting courses Repeat requests from the same department; department feedback on collaboration quality Standardization s Reusability: Design tools, templates and frameworks built and adopted across course projects Number of reusable design assets created; consistency of course quality across departments Learner Outcomes: Evidence that courses actually build the intended competencies, not just deliver information Post-course assessment results; on-the-job competency feedback from department heads Benchmark Positioning: Progress toward SCEH courses being recognized as a benchmark within the eyecare training ecosystem External faculty engagement secured; courses referenced or adapted by other institutions; recognition or adoption outside SCEH Pilot s Iteration Cycle: Speed and rigor with which new courses are piloted, evaluated and revised before scaling Time from pilot cohort completion to revised, scale-ready version Qualifications s Experience: • PhD or Postgraduate qualifycation in instructional design, education, curriculum development, adult learning, or a closely related field. A background in health sciences or public health with non-profit background is a strong plus given the clinical C support function content this role will touch and the sector that it will work with. • 6 to 10 years of experience in curriculum or course design, ideally with exposure to clinical, healthcare, or non-profit training environments. • Demonstrated experience converting subject matter expertise (from clinicians, technical experts, or specialists) into structured, learner-centered courses. • Experience working with faculty or SMEs who are excellent at their craft but not trained educators and the patience and skill to bridge that gap. • Familiarity with competency-based education and outcome-based curriculum design is essential, not optional. Skills s Competencies: • Strong grasp of instructional design principles, adult learning theory and competency mapping. • Ability to hold two roles at once: architect (defining course structure) and editor (refining content for instructional quality). • Comfortable working across very different departments, from highly technical clinical training to soft-skills or administrative training, without treating them the same way. • Strong written and verbal communication, since much of this role is translating between subject experts and learners. • Project management discipline to run several course-design projects at different stages simultaneously. • Intellectual curiosity about global best practices in professional training, balanced with respect for what SCEH already does well.

We are made up of government and non-government agencies, charities, donors and funders, professional groups, patient groups and civil society organisations. We bring together clinicians, managers, policy makers, front-line workers and implementers, scientists, patients and survivors, advocates and civil society. The Union’s Vision: A healthier world for all, free of tuberculosis and lung disease The Union’s Mission: The Union strives to end suffering due to tuberculosis and lung disease by advancing better prevention and care. We seek to achieve this by the generation, dissemination and implementation of knowledge into policy and practice. We aim to ensure that no-one is left behind, people are treated equally and we have a focus on vulnerable and marginalised populations and communities. The Union’s Values: • Quality: we deliver our services and products to the highest possible standards. • Transparency: we are open and direct in our dealings. • Accountability: we are responsible stewards of resources, deliver on our commitments, and are accountable to our stakeholders. • Respect: we recognise people’s intrinsic value and have due regard for the welfare, beliefs, perceptions, customs and cultural heritage of those we deal with. • Independence: we seek to pursue our mission free from interference by conflicts of interest. About the Project: India with an estimated 2.8 million incident TB cases and 315,000 deaths in 2023 is the highest TB burden country in the world. India’s National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) has set ambitious targets to reduce the TB incidence rate by 80% and the number of TB deaths by 90% by the year 2025 relative to 2015. With a TB prevalence of 747 per lakh and prevalence of TB Infection of 61% (57– 65%), Delhi has the highest burden of TB in India. The National TB Prevalence Survey, 2019, has revealed that, in Delhi, a majority of 69% did not seek care for their TB symptoms. The union has been implementing community-based screening (ACF) in Delhi focusing on early case finding across multiple slums and vulnerable population of Delhi in 6 NTEP districts (Narela, BJRM, Nehru Nagar, Shastri Park, Karawal Nagar and Moti Nagar). Under the project of ‘Delhi urban Health Initiative’, we have deployed 21 units of Artificial Intelligence enabled ultra-portable handheld X ray machines, with radiographers and field officers to operate the same, linked with an efficient sputum specimen collection and transportation system to ensure the completion of the cascade of care for all persons diagnosed with TB efficiently, thereby rapidly bringing down the burden of TB and deaths due to TB in Delhi. 3. SCOPE OF WORK The Consultant, Radiographer has to operate an ultraportable handheld X-ray machine fitted with Computer Assisted Diagnostics (CAD) software and Picture Archiving and Communications System (PACs). The project will be screening vulnerable population using these X-ray machines in a mix of community camps and primary health facilities. While the machines are relatively new and complete expertise is not a prerequisite since training shall be conducted for the same, the ideal candidate is expected to be well-versed with X-ray equipment operability and should possess excellent demonstrated patient handling ability. They should be able to function independently, be self-motivated, can thrive in challenging environments, willing to travel, and have a strong commitment to excellence. • Handling of the ultraportable X-ray machine unit. The unit including generator, detector, CAD software, lead aprons (if available), frames etc will be transported in a compact bag to and from camp locations to its stationing facility. Maintenance, transportation, and safekeeping of the X ray unit will be the responsibility of the radiographer. • Maintaining TLD badges including coordinating to ensure TLD badges are sent for renewal in each quarter with the agency • Handling queries from patients and offering pre-procedure guidance • Using radiographic equipment, including surgical and portable equipment, to do x-rays, and labelling them appropriately. • Monitoring the radiographic equipment and supplies and ensuring there are sufficient supplies by submitting purchase requests proactively • Maintaining stock register for the camp. • Ensuring the maintenance of X-ray machines and other related equipment. Coordinating with relevant stakeholders for AMC and any corrective/ preventive maintenance required • Documenting, recording, and storage of patient data. This includes filling up deployment forms at the beginning of the camp services for each camp location, ensure filling in complete information of clients on Qure AI • Performing end of day tasks and reporting • Holding all patient Protected Health Information (PHI), other patients’ personal information and agency information in confidence, in accordance with the Employee Confidentiality Statement. • Support project team in organizing camps at project site and mobilizing communities for X-ray screening. • Any other work assigned by the Supervisor/ Project Lead/ Project Team/Head of Office. 4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualifications and Experience: • Graduate with diploma in X-Ray technician from Government authorized college/university. • 1 to 3 years of experience • Experience in managing portable/ X-ray machines is desirable. • Proficient in MS Office with a strong command of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint. • Experience working with National health programs/ community settings will be advantageous. • Willing to travel extensively in the field. Skills and Competencies: • Good communication skills • Stakeholder Management • Work effectively within a team environment • Good interpersonal skills including problem solving skills • Detail-oriented with the ability to work independently. • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications including Excel, Word and Outlook. • Ability to plan, set priorities, handle multiple tasks under tight deadlines. Compensation offered: Offer shall be commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate. How to apply: Interested candidates must send their latest resume/CV and cover letter mentioning their motivation for the job and the specific skills and experience that makes them suitable for the job. Last date for submitting applications is 31 August 2026 and required to be sent to careers.usea@theunion.org indicating “Application for Radiographer” in the subject line. You must also submit the Job Application Form (to be filled online at https://goo.gl/forms/hchmlnx4QzdbJBRx1) before the deadline. Please note that applications submitted without the Job Application Form will not be accepted. The Union is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified women candidates are encouraged to apply. Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted.
